sections.subtitle: Zrno koje postaje stablo: poziv na zajedničku molitvu
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar pozdravlja gledatelje i slušatelje medija Ora et labora i najavljuje evanđelje dana
sections.content:
Stotu dvadesetu epizodu emisije, naslovljenu **„Milosrđe Božje – Kako raste kraljevstvo Božje?“**, voditelj **Vladimir Grebenar** otvara kratkim pozdravom „u Gospodinu“ upućenim gledateljima i slušateljima medija **Ora et labora**. Već u prvim sekundama otkriva središnju misao dana: današnje evanđelje govori o tome kako **zrno uzraste i razvije se u stablo**.

Ta slika malenog, gotovo neprimjetnog početka koji s vremenom donosi velik plod okvir je cijele epizode. Prije nego što se posveti tumačenju svete riječi, Grebenar vodi vjernike kroz dug i strukturiran molitveni program. Program počinje znakom križa, „U ime Oca i Sina i Duha Svetoga“, a nastavlja se nizom molitava zaštite, posveta, Krunicom Božjega milosrđa, litanijama i Gospinom krunicom.
sections.subtitle_en: A grain that becomes a tree: a call to common prayer
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar greets the viewers and listeners of the media outlet Ora et labora and announces the Gospel of the day
sections.content_en:
The hundred and twentieth episode of the show, titled **"Divine Mercy – How Does the Kingdom of God Grow?"**, host **Vladimir Grebenar** opens with a brief greeting "in the Lord" addressed to the viewers and listeners of the media outlet **Ora et labora**. Already in the first seconds, he reveals the central thought of the day: today's Gospel speaks of how **a grain grows and develops into a tree**.

That image of a small, almost imperceptible beginning that over time bears great fruit is the framework of the entire episode. Before dedicating himself to the interpretation of the holy word, Grebenar leads the faithful through a long and structured prayer program. The program begins with the Sign of the Cross, "In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit", and continues with a series of prayers of protection, consecrations, the Chaplet of Divine Mercy, litanies, and Our Lady's Rosary.

sections.subtitle: Molitva oslobođenja: vezanje zlih sila i zaštita Kristove krvi
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj izgovara molitvu oslobođenja kojom u ime Isusovo vezuje zle sile
sections.content:
Prva molitva u nizu izrazito je zaštitnog karaktera. Grebenar je izgovara u ime zajednice i u ime Isusovo „uzima vlast“ te **vezuje sve zle sile i snage**. Pritom ih izričito nabraja po mjestima na kojima mogu djelovati:

- u zraku,
- na zemlji,
- u vodi,
- u podzemlju,
- na onome svijetu,
- u prirodi i u vatri.

Molitva potom prelazi u hvalu: Gospodin se ispovijeda kao „Gospodin nad svim svemirom“, a slava mu se daje „u ime tvoga stvorenja“. Slijedi ključni zaziv kojim se vezuju sve demonske sile „koje su došle protiv nas i naših obitelji“. Svi se zatim stavljaju **pod zaštitu dragocjene krvi** prolivene na križu.

Osobito se moli za obitelji. Marija se zaziva kao majka, od nje se traži zagovor kod **Presvetog Srca Isusova** i moli je se da vjernike „zaogrne svojim plaštem ljubavi da se prestraši neprijatelj“. Na pomoć se poziva i **sveti Mihovil** s anđelima čuvarima, da brane vjernike „u borbi protiv svega zla što obilazi svijetom“.

Molitva doseže vrhunac zapoviješću, izrečenom u ime Isusovo, da sve sile zla „odstupe istog časa“ od molitelja, njihovih domova i njihove zemlje. Završava zahvalom Isusu kao „vjernom Bogu“ koji „osjeća s nama“.
sections.subtitle_en: Prayer of deliverance: binding evil forces and protection of Christ's blood
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host utters a prayer of deliverance by which in the name of Jesus he binds evil forces
sections.content_en:
The first prayer in the series is distinctly protective in character. Grebenar utters it in the name of the community and in the name of Jesus "takes authority" and **binds all evil forces and powers**. In doing so, he explicitly enumerates them by the places in which they can act:

- in the air,
- on the earth,
- in the water,
- in the underworld,
- in the other world,
- in nature and in fire.

The prayer then transitions into praise: the Lord is confessed as the "Lord over all the universe", and glory is given to him "in the name of your creation". There follows a key invocation binding all demonic forces "that have come against us and our families". Everyone is then placed **under the protection of the precious blood** shed on the cross.

Prayer is made especially for families. Mary is invoked as mother, intercession is asked of her before the **Sacred Heart of Jesus**, and she is asked to "cloak believers with her mantle of love so that the enemy may be terrified". **Saint Michael** with the guardian angels is also called upon for help, to defend believers "in the battle against all evil that roams the world".

The prayer reaches its climax with a command, spoken in the name of Jesus, that all forces of evil "depart this very hour" from the intercessors, their homes, and their land. It concludes with thanksgiving to Jesus as the "faithful God" who "feels with us".

sections.subtitle: Vojvoda nebeske vojske i molitva za srce koje kuca s Isusovim
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj nakon molitve svetom Mihaelu izgovara molitvu jedinstva s Isusom
sections.content:
Na molitvu oslobođenja nastavlja se tradicionalna **molitva svetom Mihaelu arkanđelu**. U njoj se arkanđeo moli da brani vjernike „u boju“ i bude im „zaklon“ od pakosti i zasjeda đavolskih. Mihael se oslovljava kao **„vojvoda vojske nebeske“** i moli se da Sotonu i druge zle duhove, koji „svijetom obilaze na propast duša“, božanskom krjepošću strovali u pakao.

Zatim tonovi borbe ustupaju mjesto nježnoj, intimnoj **molitvi jedinstva s Isusom**. Ona počinje zazivom „Moj ljupki Isuse“ i niže slike potpunog sjedinjenja čovjeka s Kristom:

- da noge zajedno hode,
- da ruke budu skupljene u jedinstvu,
- da srca kucaju zajedno,
- da duše budu u skladu, a misli kao jedno,
- da uši zajedno slušaju tišinu,
- da pogledi duboko prodru jedan u drugi.

Sve te molbe vode prema jednom cilju: da usne zajedno mole kako bi se **„zadobilo milosrđe od vječnoga Oca“**. Tako se već u uvodnom dijelu najavljuje milosrđe, glavna tema epizode.
sections.subtitle_en: Prince of the heavenly host and a prayer for a heart that beats with Jesus's
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host, after the prayer to Saint Michael, recites the prayer of unity with Jesus
sections.content_en:
The prayer of deliverance is followed by the traditional **prayer to Saint Michael the Archangel**. In it, the archangel is asked to defend believers "in battle" and be their "safeguard" against the wickedness and snares of the devil. Michael is addressed as the **"Prince of the heavenly host"** and is asked by divine power to cast into hell Satan and other evil spirits who "prowl around the world for the ruin of souls".

Then the tones of battle give way to a gentle, intimate **prayer of unity with Jesus**. It begins with the invocation "My lovely Jesus" and strings together images of the complete union of man with Christ:

- that feet walk together,
- that hands be gathered in unity,
- that hearts beat together,
- that souls be in harmony, and thoughts as one,
- that ears listen to the silence together,
- that gazes penetrate deeply into one another.

All these petitions lead toward one goal: that lips pray together in order to **"obtain mercy from the eternal Father"**. Thus, already in the introductory part, mercy is announced, the main theme of the episode.

sections.subtitle: Dvostruka posveta: Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu i Presvetom Srcu Isusovu
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar izgovara molitvu posvete Bezgrešnom Srcu Marijinu
sections.content:
Uvodni molitveni blok zaokružuju dvije posvete. U prvoj se vjernik obraća **Presvetoj Djevici Mariji** kao „majci i kraljici“. Njezinu bezgrešnom srcu posvećuje „čitavo svoje biće, svoje misli, riječi i djela“ i stavlja joj na raspolaganje sve što mu pripada, „sada i u vječnosti“. Cilj posvete jasno je izrečen: hvala i slava Presvetoga Trojstva, posvećenje Crkve i spasenje svega svijeta.

Posveta ima i vrlo osobnu dimenziju. Od Marije se traži pomoć da molitelj živi dostojno svoga **krsnog posvećenja**, da „neopozivo pripada svome Otkupitelju“ i da poput nje sluša poticaje Duha Svetoga. Završava molbom da se „u meni i u svemu vrši volja Božja“.

Druga je posveta upućena **Presvetom Srcu Isusovu**, koje se naziva „izvorom svakoga dobra“. Molitelj mu se klanja, ispovijeda vjeru i ufanje, izražava ljubav i kaje se za grijehe. Zatim mu poklanja svoje „siromašno srce“ i moli da ga Isus učini **poniznim, strpljivim i čistim**. Slijedi niz konkretnih molbi:

- da Isus živi u njemu i on u Isusu,
- zaštita u opasnostima,
- utjeha u nevoljama i žalostima,
- zdravlje tijela,
- blagoslov svega rada,
- milost svete smrti.

Odmah nakon toga Grebenar najavljuje sljedeću cjelinu i poziva vjernike: „Sklopimo oči, priđimo milosrdnom Gospodinu.“
sections.subtitle_en: Double consecration: to the Immaculate Heart of Mary and the Sacred Heart of Jesus
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar utters the prayer of consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary
sections.content_en:
The introductory prayer block is rounded off by two consecrations. In the first, the believer addresses the **Blessed Virgin Mary** as "mother and queen". To her immaculate heart he consecrates "his entire being, his thoughts, words, and deeds" and places at her disposal everything that belongs to him, "now and in eternity". The goal of the consecration is clearly stated: the praise and glory of the Most Holy Trinity, the sanctification of the Church, and the salvation of the whole world.

The consecration also has a very personal dimension. Mary is asked for help so that the person praying lives worthily of his **baptismal consecration**, "irrevocably belongs to his Redeemer", and like her listens to the promptings of the Holy Spirit. It ends with a petition that "in me and in everything the will of God be done".

The second consecration is addressed to the **Sacred Heart of Jesus**, which is called the "source of every good". The person praying adores it, confesses faith and hope, expresses love, and repents of sins. Then he gifts it his "poor heart" and prays that Jesus make it **humble, patient, and pure**. A series of concrete petitions follows:

- that Jesus live in him and he in Jesus,
- protection in dangers,
- comfort in tribulations and sorrows,
- health of body,
- blessing of all work,
- the grace of a holy death.

Immediately after that, Grebenar announces the next section and invites the faithful: "Let us close our eyes, let us approach the merciful Lord."

sections.subtitle: Krunica Božjega milosrđa: „Po njegovoj pregorkoj muci“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj predmolitvom „Vječni Oče, prikazujemo ti tijelo i krv…“ započinje prvu deseticu Krunice Božjega milosrđa
sections.content:
Središnji dio prve trećine emisije čini **Krunica Božjega milosrđa**. Grebenar je započinje molitvama **Oče naš**, **Zdravo Marijo** i **Vjerujem**. U Apostolskom vjerovanju ispovijeda se vjera u Boga Oca Stvoritelja te u Isusa Krista, „mučena pod Poncijem Pilatom“, raspeta, umrla, pokopana i uskrsla. Ispovijeda se i vjera u Duha Svetoga, svetu Crkvu katoličku, općinstvo svetih, oproštenje grijeha, uskrsnuće tijela i život vječni.

Svaka od pet desetica počinje istom prikaznom molitvom:

> „Vječni Oče, prikazujemo ti tijelo i krv, dušu i božanstvo preljubljenoga Sina tvojega, Gospodina našega Isusa Krista, kao zadovoljštinu za grijehe naše i cijeloga svijeta.“

Nakon nje deset se puta ponavlja zaziv **„Po njegovoj pregorkoj muci, budi milosrdan nama i cijelome svijetu.“** Ritmičko ponavljanje molitvi daje meditativan, gotovo hipnotički tok. Zaziv ne traži milosrđe samo za molitelja, nego izričito i za „cijeli svijet“.

Krunica završava zazivima koji se ponavljaju tri puta: **„Sveti Bože, sveti jaki Bože, sveti besmrtni Bože, smiluj se nama i cijelomu svijetu.“** Slijedi zaziv **„O krvi i vodo, što potekoste iz Srca Isusova kao izvor milosrđa za nas, uzdam se u tebe“**, zatim molitva „Marijo, majko milosrđa, moli za nas“. Tri puta ponovljen poklik **„Isuse, uzdam se u tebe“** zatvara ovaj dio.
sections.subtitle_en: Chaplet of Divine Mercy: "For the sake of His sorrowful Passion"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host begins the first decade of the Chaplet of Divine Mercy with the opening prayer "Eternal Father, we offer you the Body and Blood…"
sections.content_en:
The central part of the first third of the show is the **Chaplet of Divine Mercy**. Grebenar begins it with the prayers **Our Father**, **Hail Mary**, and the **Creed**. In the Apostles' Creed, faith is professed in God the Father Creator and in Jesus Christ, "suffered under Pontius Pilate", crucified, died, buried, and risen. Faith is also professed in the Holy Spirit, the holy Catholic Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and life everlasting.

Each of the five decades begins with the same offering prayer:

> "Eternal Father, we offer you the Body and Blood, Soul and Divinity of your dearly beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, in atonement for our sins and those of the whole world."

After it, the invocation **"For the sake of His sorrowful Passion, have mercy on us and on the whole world."** is repeated ten times. The rhythmic repetition of the prayers gives a meditative, almost hypnotic flow. The invocation does not seek mercy only for the one praying, but explicitly also for the "whole world".

The Chaplet ends with invocations repeated three times: **"Holy God, Holy Mighty God, Holy Immortal God, have mercy on us and on the whole world."** There follows the invocation **"O Blood and Water, which gushed forth from the Heart of Jesus as a fount of mercy for us, I trust in You"**, then the prayer "Mary, Mother of Mercy, pray for us". The exclamation **"Jesus, I trust in You"**, repeated three times, closes this part.

sections.subtitle: Gospina krunica: od krvavog znoja do bičevanja i trnove krune
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj najavljuje prvo žalosno otajstvo: „koji se za nas krvavim znojem znojio“
sections.content:
Riječima „Slijedi Gospina krunica“ Grebenar uvodi vjernike u molitvu **žalosnih otajstava**, koja prate Kristovu muku. Svako otajstvo ima istu strukturu:

- najava otajstva,
- molitva **Oče naš**,
- deset puta **Zdravo Marijo**,
- **Slava Ocu**,
- završni zaziv **„O moj Isuse, oprosti nam naše grijehe, očuvaj nas od paklenoga ognja, dovedi u raj sve duše, a osobito one kojima je najpotrebnije tvoje milosrđe.“**

**Prvo otajstvo**, „koji se za nas krvavim znojem znojio“, vodi u Isusovu borbu prije muke. Nakon njega dolazi **drugo otajstvo**, „koji je za nas bio bičevan“, posvećeno fizičkom mučenju Krista. **Treće otajstvo**, „koji je za nas trnjem bio okrunjen“, podsjeća na ruganje i poniženje kojima je Isus bio izložen.

Izraz „za nas“, koji se ponavlja u svakoj najavi, naglašava da se Kristova patnja promatra kao čin podnesen radi čovjeka. Završni zaziv svake desetice ponovno se vraća temi milosrđa, u čijem je znaku cijela emisija.
sections.subtitle_en: Our Lady's Rosary: from the bloody sweat to the scourging and the crown of thorns
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host announces the first sorrowful mystery: „who sweated blood for us“
sections.content_en:
With the words „Our Lady's Rosary follows“ Grebenar introduces the faithful into the prayer of the **sorrowful mysteries**, which follow Christ's Passion. Each mystery has the same structure:

- announcement of the mystery,
- the **Our Father** prayer,
- ten times the **Hail Mary**,
- the **Glory Be**,
- the concluding invocation **„O my Jesus, forgive us our sins, save us from the fires of hell, lead all souls to heaven, especially those most in need of your mercy.“**

**The first mystery**, „who sweated blood for us“, leads into Jesus's struggle before the Passion. After it comes **the second mystery**, „who was scourged for us“, dedicated to the physical torture of Christ. **The third mystery**, „who was crowned with thorns for us“, recalls the mockery and humiliation to which Jesus was subjected.

The phrase „for us“, which is repeated in each announcement, emphasizes that Christ's suffering is viewed as an act endured for the sake of man. The concluding invocation of each decade returns again to the theme of mercy, in whose sign the entire broadcast is.

sections.subtitle: Križni put do Golgote: nošenje križa i raspeće
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar najavljuje peto žalosno otajstvo: „koji je za nas bio razapet“
sections.content:
Drugi dio krunice prati vrhunac Kristove muke. **Četvrto otajstvo**, „koji je za nas teški križ nosio“, prikazuje Isusov put pod teretom križa. Riječ „teški“ u najavi posebno ističe težinu tereta.

**Peto otajstvo**, „koji je za nas bio razapet“, zaključuje niz razmatranja žalosnih otajstava. Kao i prethodna, moli se kroz Oče naš, deset Zdravo Marija i Slava Ocu.

I ovdje svaku deseticu zatvara molitva u kojoj se od Isusa traži oproštenje grijeha, očuvanje od paklenoga ognja te spasenje svih duša, „a osobito onih kojima je najpotrebnije tvoje milosrđe“. Tako se na kraju razmatranja muke ponovno spaja motiv Kristove žrtve s temom Božjeg milosrđa, koja povezuje sve dijelove ove molitvene cjeline.
sections.subtitle_en: The Way of the Cross to Golgotha: Carrying of the Cross and Crucifixion
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar announces the fifth Sorrowful Mystery: „who was crucified for us“
sections.content_en:
The second part of the Rosary follows the culmination of Christ's Passion. **The fourth mystery**, „who carried the heavy cross for us“, depicts Jesus' path under the burden of the cross. The word „heavy“ in the announcement particularly emphasizes the weight of the burden.

**The fifth mystery**, „who was crucified for us“, concludes the series of meditations on the Sorrowful Mysteries. Like the previous ones, it is prayed through the Our Father, ten Hail Marys, and the Glory Be.

Here too, each decade is closed by a prayer in which Jesus is asked for the forgiveness of sins, preservation from the fire of hell, and the salvation of all souls, „and especially those who are in most need of your mercy“. Thus, at the end of the meditation on the Passion, the motif of Christ's sacrifice is once again joined with the theme of God's mercy, which connects all parts of this prayer whole.

sections.subtitle: „Zdravo Kraljice“ i prijelaz na tumačenje svete riječi
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj moli „Zdravo Kraljice“ i najavljuje tumačenje svete riječi
sections.content:
Molitveni dio emisije završava antifonom **„Zdravo Kraljice“**. Marija se u njoj pozdravlja kao „majka milosrđa“ te „život, slast i ufanje naše“. Vjernici joj vapiju kao „prognani sinovi Evini“ koji „tuguju i plaču u ovoj suznoj dolini“.

Molitva završava molbom zagovornici da na ljude svrne „one svoje milostive oči“ i da im „poslije ovoga progona“ pokaže Isusa, „blagoslovljeni plod utrobe svoje“. Zatvara je trostrukim zazivom: **„O blaga, o mila, o slatka Djevice Marijo.“**

Nakon gotovo četrdeset minuta neprekinute molitve, od molitava zaštite i posveta preko Krunice Božjega milosrđa i litanija do Gospine krunice, Vladimir Grebenar najavljuje sljedeći dio emisije riječima: **„Slijedi tumačenje svete riječi.“**
sections.subtitle_en: "Hail, Holy Queen" and transition to the interpretation of the holy word
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host prays the "Hail, Holy Queen" and announces the interpretation of the holy word
sections.content_en:
The prayer part of the broadcast ends with the antiphon **"Hail, Holy Queen"**. In it, Mary is greeted as the "mother of mercy" and "our life, our sweetness, and our hope". The faithful cry out to her as "banished children of Eve" who "mourn and weep in this valley of tears".

The prayer ends with a petition to the advocate to turn "those merciful eyes of hers" toward people and "after this exile" show them Jesus, "the blessed fruit of her womb". It closes with the threefold invocation: **"O clement, o loving, o sweet Virgin Mary."**

After nearly forty minutes of uninterrupted prayer, from prayers of protection and consecrations through the Chaplet of Divine Mercy and litanies to Our Lady's Rosary, Vladimir Grebenar announces the next part of the broadcast with the words: **"The interpretation of the holy word follows."**

sections.subtitle: „Otajstvo je to veliko“: brak kao zrcalo odnosa Krista i Crkve
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar, nakon čitanja Poslanice Efežanima, ističe Pavlove riječi „Otajstvo je to veliko“
sections.content:
Tumačenje svete riječi **Vladimir Grebenar**, voditelj podcasta Ora et labora, započinje čitanjem odlomka iz Poslanice Efežanima. U tekstu sveti Pavao poziva vjernike: **„Braćo, podložni budite jedni drugima u strahu Kristovu.“** Ženama poručuje da budu podložne svojim muževima kao Gospodinu jer je muž glava žene kao što je Krist glava Crkve. Muževima pak nalaže da ljube svoje žene kao što je Krist ljubio Crkvu i sebe predao za nju, da je posveti i predvede sebi „slavnu, bez ljage i nabora“. Odlomak završava starozavjetnim citatom o čovjeku koji ostavlja oca i majku da prione uz svoju ženu, nakon čega slijedi Pavlov zaključak: **„Otajstvo je to veliko. Ja smjeram na Krista i na Crkvu.“**

Grebenar kaže da mu upravo ta rečenica posebno odzvanja u srcu. Ističe da sveti Pavao nije imao ženu, a ipak se divi tom otajstvu. Prema njegovu tumaču, apostol zapravo uspoređuje **dva velika otajstva**. Prvo je bračno otajstvo, koje voditelj naziva „manjim“, uz izričitu napomenu da time ne misli reći nevažnim: ono je „jako, jako važno“, ali ipak manje od otajstva između Krista i Crkve.

Upravo bi to drugo otajstvo, naglašava Grebenar, moralo biti temelj na nekoliko razina:

- **osobnog života** svakog vjernika,
- **života obitelji**,
- **života naroda**,
- i naposljetku **čitavog svijeta**.

U tom odnosu Krist je zaručnik, a Crkva zaručnica. Voditelj objašnjava da Pavao ovdje opisuje ono što se očekuje na kraju vremena, Isusov drugi dolazak, kada će Krist primiti svoju Crkvu „bez ljage, bez mane“. Bračnu ljubav između muža i žene apostol koristi kao usporedbu kojom vjernicima približava tu eshatološku stvarnost.
sections.subtitle_en: "This is a great mystery": marriage as a mirror of the relationship between Christ and the Church
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar, after reading the Epistle to the Ephesians, highlights Paul's words "This is a great mystery"
sections.content_en:
The interpretation of the holy word **Vladimir Grebenar**, host of the podcast Ora et labora, begins by reading a passage from the Epistle to the Ephesians. In the text, Saint Paul calls the faithful: **"Brothers, be subordinate to one another in the fear of Christ."** He tells wives to be subordinate to their husbands as to the Lord, because the husband is the head of the wife as Christ is the head of the Church. To husbands, on the other hand, he commands to love their wives as Christ loved the Church and gave himself up for her, to sanctify her and present her to himself "glorious, without spot or wrinkle". The passage ends with an Old Testament quotation about a man leaving his father and mother to cling to his wife, followed by Paul's conclusion: **"This is a great mystery. I refer to Christ and the Church."**

Grebenar says that precisely this sentence resonates especially in his heart. He points out that Saint Paul did not have a wife, yet he still marvels at this mystery. According to his interpretation, the apostle is actually comparing **two great mysteries**. The first is the mystery of marriage, which the host calls "lesser", with the explicit note that by this he does not mean unimportant: it is "very, very important", but nevertheless lesser than the mystery between Christ and the Church.

Precisely this second mystery, Grebenar emphasizes, would have to be the foundation on several levels:

- **personal life** of every believer,
- **family life**,
- **life of the nation**,
- and ultimately **of the entire world**.

In this relationship, Christ is the bridegroom, and the Church is the bride. The host explains that Paul here describes what is expected at the end of time, Jesus's second coming, when Christ will receive his Church "without spot, without blemish". The apostle uses marital love between husband and wife as a comparison by which he brings this eschatological reality closer to the faithful.

sections.subtitle: Jedno tijelo i jedan duh: od bračnog čina do slike Presvetog Trojstva
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar uspoređuje bračno jedinstvo s jedinstvom Oca, Sina i Duha Svetoga
sections.content:
Pavao se poziva na sam početak Svetog pisma: **„Ostavit će čovjek oca i majku i prionuti uz svoju ženu i bit će njih dvoje jedno tijelo.“** Grebenar iz toga izvodi da je bračni čin između muškarca i žene sjedinjenje dvoje ljudi u jedno tijelo. Priznaje da prirodne oči i dalje vide dvoje ljudi, „dva tijela koja hodaju“. Sveto pismo je, međutim, po njegovim riječima **duhovna knjiga** koja otkriva duhovnu pozadinu života. Ljudi tu pozadinu ne vide jer su zaslijepljeni grijesima, tamom svijeta i vlastitim slabostima. Onima koji rastu u vjeri i primaju „milost na milost“ oči se postupno otvaraju za razumijevanje Božje riječi, jer je „sve stvoreno po riječi“.

Kada se muškarac i žena sjedine u bračnom činu onako kako je Bog zapovjedio, tumači voditelj, oni pred Bogom postaju **jedno tijelo i jedan duh**. Ljudi u grijehu to ne vide, ali Bog vidi muža i ženu kao jedno tijelo. To je za njega jedinstvo u braku: dvije osobe, ali jedno tijelo.

Ovo jedinstvo Grebenar naziva **slikom Presvetog Trojstva**. Otac i Sin dvije su božanske osobe, a jedan Bog, dok je ljubav koja izlazi između njih Duh Sveti. „Tri osobe, Trojstvo, jedan Bog“, ponavlja voditelj i naglašava koliko je to jedinstvo neraskidivo. Takvo jedinstvo, kaže, nije od ovoga svijeta i nije plod ljudskih nastojanja da se bude dobar sa svima ili s nekima.

### Košarkaški tim kao zemaljska usporedba

Da bi pojasnio razliku, Grebenar se poziva na vlastito sportsko iskustvo. U košarkaškom timu jedinstvo je presudno: igrači moraju djelovati zajedno, poznavati kretnje i biti sinkronizirani onako kako je trener zamislio. Na tome se radi iz treninga u trening, a dobar trener zna da je izgrađeno jedinstvo **formula za uspjeh i pobjede**. No to je, napominje, jedinstvo tijela, ono što se vidi očima. U duhovnom svijetu postoji dublje, duhovno jedinstvo, a takvo je i sjedinjenje muškarca i žene koji postaju jedno tijelo. Zaključuje da bi tome trebalo poučavati mlade i vlastitu djecu.
sections.subtitle_en: One Body and One Spirit: From the Marital Act to the Image of the Most Holy Trinity
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar compares marital unity to the unity of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit
sections.content_en:
Paul refers to the very beginning of Sacred Scripture: **“A man will leave his father and mother and cling to his wife, and the two shall be one body.”** Grebenar deduces from this that the marital act between a man and a woman is the union of two people into one body. He admits that natural eyes still see two people, “two bodies walking”. Sacred Scripture is, however, according to his words, **a spiritual book** that reveals the spiritual background of life. People do not see that background because they are blinded by sins, the darkness of the world, and their own weaknesses. To those who grow in faith and receive “grace upon grace”, their eyes gradually open to the understanding of God's word, because “everything was created through the word”.

When a man and a woman unite in the marital act in the way God commanded, the host explains, before God they become **one body and one spirit**. People in sin do not see this, but God sees husband and wife as one body. For him, this is unity in marriage: two persons, but one body.

Grebenar calls this unity **an image of the Most Holy Trinity**. The Father and the Son are two divine persons, and one God, while the love proceeding between them is the Holy Spirit. “Three persons, Trinity, one God,” repeats the host and emphasizes how indissoluble this unity is. Such unity, he says, is not of this world and is not the fruit of human efforts to be good with everyone or with some.

### Basketball Team as an Earthly Comparison

To clarify the difference, Grebenar refers to his own sporting experience. In a basketball team, unity is crucial: the players must act together, know the movements, and be synchronized the way the coach envisioned. This is worked on from practice to practice, and a good coach knows that built unity is **the formula for success and victories**. But that, he notes, is unity of the body, what is seen with the eyes. In the spiritual world there is a deeper, spiritual unity, and such is the union of a man and a woman who become one body. He concludes that young people and one's own children should be taught this.

sections.subtitle: Predbračni odnosi i „mijenjanje partnera“: put nezadovoljstva prema Grebenarovu tumačenju
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o posljedicama spolnog grijeha i rastućoj požudi
sections.content:
Grebenar zatim razlikuje dvoje mladih koji „šetaju i hodaju“ i tada su još dva odvojena tijela i dvije odvojene osobe, od stanja nakon spolnog čina. Bog čovjeku daje slobodu jer ima povjerenja u njega, kaže voditelj. Ipak, i **predbračni odnos** po njegovu tumaču sjedinjuje dvoje ljudi u jedno tijelo, samo ne na svet, nego na grešan način. Takav čin, tvrdi, ne može donijeti blagoslov, radost, mir ni milost, nego samo nezadovoljstvo.

Iz toga izvodi tezu o onima, mladima i starima, koji „mijenjaju partnere“, kako se to danas kaže. Njihovo srce, duh i tijelo ostaju nezadovoljeni pa nastavljaju tražiti. Voditelj kaže da mu je tužno gledati kako su mnogi muškarci i žene „podali svoje tijelo“ u potrazi za ispunjenjem koje je u stvarnosti, po njegovim riječima, „sve dublje propadanje“.

### Teza o rastućoj požudi i generacijskom nasljeđu

U nastavku Grebenar iznosi svoje uvjerenje da ustrajno spolno griješenje vodi prema sve jačim požudama. Polazi od biblijske misli da onaj tko čini grijeh postaje rob grijeha. Prema njegovu tumačenju, đavao tada „pali vatru pakla“ u čovjeku, vatru požude koja postaje jača od same osobe. Ljudi tada ulaze u preljube i „spavaju svako sa svakim“. Ako ne dođe do pokajanja i prekida, nastavlja voditelj, to u konačnici vodi do homoseksualnosti, koju on naziva sodomijom i ubraja među njezine uzroke.

Voditelj dodaje i tvrdnju o **generacijskom nasljeđu**. Prema njegovu mišljenju, posljedice takvog načina života mogu se „kroz generacijsko stablo“ spustiti na djecu, unuke i praunuke, pa netko rođen „nedužan“ kasnije kaže da ima takve sklonosti, iako nitko ne zna što su radili djed i baka.

### „Ne osuditi, nego navijestiti lijek“

Iako je dio izlaganja oštar, Grebenar ovu cjelinu zaključuje porukom o odnosu prema konkretnim ljudima. **Osobe s takvim sklonostima ne treba osuđivati**, kaže, nego ih treba razumjeti, jer Krist ima lijek za sve što je grijeh. Odgovornost vjernika nije osuda, nego pomoć: navijestiti im Krista i reći im da je Isus „sam lijek“. Vjernici, poručuje, trebaju donositi svjedočanstvo, Božju riječ i molitvu, „nikako osude“.
sections.subtitle_en: Premarital relations and "changing partners": a path of dissatisfaction according to Grebenar's interpretation
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about the consequences of sexual sin and growing lust
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then distinguishes two young people who "stroll and date" and are at that point still two separate bodies and two separate persons, from the state after the sexual act. God gives man freedom because He has trust in him, the host says. Nevertheless, even **premarital relations**, according to his interpretation, unite two people into one body, only not in a holy, but in a sinful way. Such an act, he claims, cannot bring blessing, joy, peace, nor grace, but only dissatisfaction.

From this, he derives a thesis about those, young and old, who "change partners," as it is said today. Their heart, spirit, and body remain unsatisfied, so they continue searching. The host says that it is sad for him to watch how many men and women have "yielded their body" in search of fulfillment that is in reality, in his words, "an ever deeper ruin."

### The thesis on growing lust and generational inheritance

Continuing, Grebenar expresses his conviction that persistent sexual sinning leads toward increasingly stronger lusts. He starts from the biblical thought that whoever commits sin becomes a slave of sin. According to his interpretation, the devil then "lights the fire of hell" in man, the fire of lust that becomes stronger than the person themselves. People then enter into adulteries and "sleep each with everyone." If repentance and a break do not occur, the host continues, this ultimately leads to homosexuality, which he calls sodomy and counts among its causes.

The host also adds a claim about **generational inheritance**. In his view, the consequences of such a lifestyle can "through the generational tree" descend upon children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren, so that someone born "innocent" later says that they have such inclinations, although no one knows what the grandfather and grandmother did.

### "Not to condemn, but to proclaim the remedy"

Although part of the presentation is harsh, Grebenar concludes this section with a message about the attitude toward concrete people. **Persons with such inclinations should not be condemned**, he says, but rather they should be understood, because Christ has a remedy for everything that is sin. The responsibility of believers is not condemnation, but help: to proclaim Christ to them and tell them that Jesus is "the remedy Himself." Believers, he conveys, should bring witness, God's word, and prayer, "by no means condemnations."

sections.subtitle: „Blago svakome koji se boji Gospodina“ i opasnost obljutavljene soli
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar svjedoči: „Ja se, braćo i sestre, bojim Gospodina“
sections.content:
Sljedeći dio tumačenja otvara psalam: **„Blago svakome koji se boji Gospodina, koji njegovim hodi stazama.“** Psalam obećava da će čovjek uživati plod ruku svojih, da će mu žena biti „kao plodna loza u odajama kuće“, a sinovi „kao mladice masline oko stola“. Završava blagoslovom sa Siona i poželjnom srećom Jeruzalema u sve dane života.

Grebenar odmah nudi osobno svjedočanstvo: **„Ja se bojim Gospodina.“** Zahvalan je Bogu na toj milosti jer ga, kako kaže, „drži jako budnim“. Zato se ne usuđuje propovijedati da se čovjek može spasiti samim time što je dobar prema drugim ljudima, a da pritom ne mari za Boga.

Voditelj kritizira ono što naziva **„bljutavim nagovorima i propovijedima“** laika i nekih klerika. Prenosi riječi jednog svećenika koje je nedavno čuo na misi: „Ako sol obljutavi, gotovo je, onda narod gazi po soli.“ Kada se biskup, svećenik, laik, otac obitelji, poduzetnik ili politički lider ne boji Gospodina, tvrdi Grebenar, njemu je sve svejedno, pa slikovito kaže da tada „može i dugina zastava na oltaru“ i da se „otvaraju vrata svima“.

Nasuprot tome stavlja Isusov primjer: Krist je **osudio grijeh, a oslobodio i izliječio grešnika**. Mnogi danas, prema voditelju, zbog nevjere i nedostatka straha Božjega ne osuđuju grijeh. Umjesto toga „u ime tolerancije“ prihvaćaju ljude koji ustraju u grijehu bez kajanja, a da im pritom ni ne navijeste Krista.

### Lobi u kršćanskim Crkvama

Grebenar tvrdi da u čitavom kršćanskom svijetu jača određeni lobi. Po njegovim riječima pojavio se najprije kod protestanata, potom je ušao u Katoličku Crkvu, a „negdje čak i kod pravoslavnih“. Sve veći broj ljudi u kleru, navodi, govori da istospolni odnosi nisu grijeh, dok on ističe da ih Sveto pismo osuđuje.

Odgovornost vjernika ovdje je, prema njegovu tumaču, ključna. Oni koji takvo stanje brane „u neznanju, u tami srca“ mogu to tako braniti pred Bogom. Kad jednom čuju od kršćana istinu i poruku da Isus ima rješenje, pred njima je slobodan izbor. Ako odbiju, vjernik je „slobodan od njihove propasti“. Ako pak vjernici prešute da je Isus osloboditelj, zaključuje voditelj, „onda smo mi krivci, braćo i sestre, za njihovu propast“.
sections.subtitle_en: “Blessed is everyone who fears the Lord” and the danger of tasteless salt
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar testifies: “Brothers and sisters, I fear the Lord”
sections.content_en:
The next part of the interpretation opens with the psalm: **“Blessed is everyone who fears the Lord, who walks in his ways.”** The psalm promises that a man will enjoy the fruit of his hands, that his wife will be “like a fruitful vine in the heart of his house,” and his sons “like olive shoots around the table.” It ends with a blessing from Zion and the desired prosperity of Jerusalem all the days of life.

Grebenar immediately offers a personal testimony: **“I fear the Lord.”** He is grateful to God for that grace because, as he says, it “keeps him very vigilant.” That is why he does not dare to preach that a man can be saved merely by being good to other people without caring about God.

The host criticizes what he calls **“tasteless exhortations and homilies”** of laity and some clerics. He conveys the words of a priest he recently heard at Mass: “If salt loses its taste, it is over, then the people trample on the salt.” When a bishop, a priest, a layman, a father of a family, an entrepreneur, or a political leader does not fear the Lord, Grebenar claims, everything is all the same to him, so he figuratively says that then “even a rainbow flag can be on the altar” and that “the doors are opened to everyone.”

In contrast to this, he places Jesus' example: Christ **condemned sin, but set free and healed the sinner**. Many today, according to the host, due to unbelief and lack of fear of God, do not condemn sin. Instead, “in the name of tolerance,” they accept people who persist in sin without repentance, without even proclaiming Christ to them.

### A lobby in Christian Churches

Grebenar claims that a certain lobby is growing stronger throughout the Christian world. In his words, it appeared first among Protestants, then entered the Catholic Church, and “somewhere even among the Orthodox.” An increasing number of people in the clergy, he states, say that same-sex relations are not a sin, while he emphasizes that Sacred Scripture condemns them.

The responsibility of believers here is, according to his interpretation, crucial. Those who defend such a state “in ignorance, in the darkness of the heart” can defend it that way before God. Once they hear the truth from Christians and the message that Jesus has a solution, a free choice lies before them. If they refuse, the believer is “free from their ruin.” If, however, believers keep silent about Jesus being the deliverer, the host concludes, “then we are guilty, brothers and sisters, of their ruin.”

sections.subtitle: Anegdota s doškolovanja: pitanje o toleranciji koje je izazvalo bijes
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar prepričava iskustvo s predavanja na pedagoškom doškolovanju
sections.content:
Govoreći o pojavi koju vidi kod dijela klera, Grebenar kaže da je riječ o „manjem dijelu, bez dileme, ali ne više ni tako malom“, i da je to sada „čitav pokret“. Takvo stanje, tvrdi, odobravaju i kršteni laici. Kritizira i to što su neke **desne, kršćanske vlade i stranke u Europi i svijetu legalizirale istospolne zajednice** kao bračne zajednice i dale im puna prava, „novcem svih nas, poreznih obveznika“.

Svoju zabrinutost voditelj opisuje slikom **trule jabuke u korpi**, od koje obolijevaju i zdrave. Tvrdi da se upravo to sada događa u društvu i da je sve više mladih učitelja i profesora, po njegovoj ocjeni većinom „indoktriniranih“, koji poučavaju djecu.

### Što se dogodilo na predavanju

Kao potvrdu navodi osobno iskustvo od prije petnaestak godina. Kako bi mogao predavati u srednjoj školi i na fakultetu, morao je položiti osam ispita iz **pedagoških razlika**. Te je ispite tražilo i nekoliko fakulteta u Hrvatskoj, a on je kasnije doista radio na fakultetu kao profesor i predavač. U to je vrijeme, prisjeća se, već imao doktorat, dok su ostali polaznici uglavnom bili studenti četvrte i pete godine, desetak i više godina mlađi od njega.

Predavala im je sveučilišna profesorica, doktorica znanosti s pedagoškog fakulteta, tek nešto starija od njega. Ostalo mu je u sjećanju kako je spomenula da njezina kći, učenica prvog ili drugog razreda srednje škole, idući vikend „treba obaviti krizmu“. Izraz „obaviti krizmu“ posebno mu je zapeo za uho.

Na jednom predavanju profesorica je poručila da budući učitelji moraju djecu i mlade učiti da istospolne odnose treba prihvatiti. Grebenara je šokiralo što se nitko od mlađih kolega nije usprotivio. Njegova bi se generacija, kaže, usprotivila. Zato je sam postavio pitanje: **„Vi kažete da treba biti tolerantan. A tko će biti tolerantan prema nama?“** Mislio je na sebe i mnoge koji to stanje smatraju grijehom.

Reakcija ga je, prema vlastitom opisu, zatekla. Imao je osjećaj „kao da su se vrata pakla otvorila“. Mladi koji su dotad šutjeli počeli su se prema njemu odnositi agresivno i s prezirom. „Ovi da će predavati mojoj djeci u školi? Pa to je pakao“, prisjeća se svoje tadašnje misli.
sections.subtitle_en: Anecdote from further education: a question about tolerance that provoked fury
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar recounts an experience from a lecture during pedagogical further education
sections.content_en:
Speaking about the phenomenon he sees among a part of the clergy, Grebenar says that it is a matter of a "smaller part, without a doubt, but no longer so small either", and that it is now an "entire movement". Such a state of affairs, he claims, is also approved by baptized laity. He also criticizes the fact that some **right-wing, Christian governments and parties in Europe and the world have legalized same-sex unions** as marital unions and given them full rights, "with the money of all of us, taxpayers".

The host describes his concern with the image of a **rotten apple in a basket**, from which the healthy ones also fall ill. He claims that this is precisely what is happening in society now and that there are more and more young teachers and professors, in his assessment mostly "indoctrinated", who are teaching children.

### What happened at the lecture

As confirmation, he cites a personal experience from about fifteen years ago. In order to be able to teach in high school and at the university, he had to pass eight exams in **pedagogical differences**. These exams were also required by several faculties in Croatia, and he later indeed worked at a faculty as a professor and lecturer. At that time, he recalls, he already had a doctorate, while the other attendees were mostly fourth- and fifth-year students, about ten or more years younger than him.

They were taught by a university professor, a doctor of science from the faculty of education, only slightly older than him. He remembered how she mentioned that her daughter, a student in the first or second year of high school, "needs to get confirmation done" the next weekend. The expression "get confirmation done" particularly caught his ear.

At one lecture, the professor stated that future teachers must teach children and young people that same-sex relationships should be accepted. Grebenar was shocked that none of the younger colleagues objected. His generation, he says, would have objected. That is why he asked the question himself: **"You say that one should be tolerant. But who will be tolerant toward us?"** He was thinking of himself and many who consider that condition to be a sin.

The reaction, according to his own description, took him by surprise. He felt "as if the gates of hell had opened". The young people who had been silent until then began to treat him aggressively and with contempt. "These people are going to teach my children in school? Why, that is hell", he recalls his thought at the time.

sections.subtitle: Podijeljene zbornice i kako opstati na radnom mjestu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj savjetuje vjernike kako se ponašati na poslu u neprijateljskom okruženju
sections.content:
Iskustvo s predavanja Grebenar povezuje s, kako kaže, „ogromnim problemom u hrvatskom društvu o kojem se ne govori“. Stariji učitelji i profesori često spominju da postoje **podjele u zbornicama**, koje bi se mogle opisati kao podjele na lijevo i desno. To je za njega slika podjele cijelog društva i svijeta.

Voditelj, međutim, poručuje da se zbog toga ne treba brinuti, jer su to **znakovi vremena**. Poziva se na Isusove riječi: **„Nisam došao donijeti mir, nego razdjeljenje.“** Smatra čak da je dobro što se ljudi dijele na Kristove i one koji to nisu, i unutar obitelji i unutar radnih kolektiva. S nekim se mogu dijeliti učionica, prostor i radno vrijeme, ali ne mora se dijeliti slobodno vrijeme. Za takve kolege treba moliti, blagoslivljati ih i navijestiti im Krista ako žele slušati. „Ako neće, ništa, pusti ga“, kaže.

### Sakramentali, molitva i post

Na često pitanje vjernika kako se ponašati na poslu u takvom okruženju, Grebenar odgovara da odgovor daju Sveto pismo i sveti Pavao: od svijeta se ne može pobjeći ni sakriti, ali milost Božja čuva čovjeka. Teret postoji, priznaje, ali postoje i rješenja:

- **sakramentali i medaljice** za zaštitu prostora,
- **molitva** za ljude s kojima se radi,
- **post**, uz savjet: „Posti, pa ćeš vidjeti promjenu.“

Svoj pristup sažima izrekom „klin se klinom izbija“ i dodaje: „Bolje da njega boli glava od utjecaja sakramentala i milosti Božje koja tebe štiti, nego da tebe boli glava od stanja grijeha i posljedica grijeha u kojem se ti ljudi nalaze.“
sections.subtitle_en: Divided staffrooms and how to survive in the workplace
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host advises believers on how to behave at work in a hostile environment
sections.content_en:
Grebenar connects the experience from the lecture with, as he says, a "huge problem in Croatian society that is not spoken about." Older teachers and professors often mention that there are **divisions in staffrooms**, which could be described as divisions into left and right. For him, this is an image of the division of the entire society and the world.

The host, however, conveys that one should not worry about this, because these are **signs of the times**. He refers to Jesus' words: **"I have not come to bring peace, but division."** He even considers it good that people are divided into Christ's and those who are not, both within families and within working collectives. With someone, a classroom, space, and working hours can be shared, but free time does not have to be shared. One should pray for such colleagues, bless them, and proclaim Christ to them if they want to listen. "If he will not, nothing, leave him alone," he says.

### Sacramentals, prayer, and fasting

To the frequent question of believers on how to behave at work in such an environment, Grebenar answers that Sacred Scripture and Saint Paul give the answer: one cannot run away or hide from the world, but the grace of God preserves a person. A burden exists, he admits, but there are also solutions:

- **sacramentals and medals** for the protection of space,
- **prayer** for the people one works with,
- **fasting**, with the advice: "Fast, and you will see a change."

He summarizes his approach with the saying "fight fire with fire" and adds: "Better that his head hurts from the influence of sacramentals and the grace of God that protects you, than that your head hurts from the state of sin and the consequences of sin in which those people find themselves."

sections.subtitle: Strah Božji nije strah od kazne: čiji sud zaista ima težinu
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar objašnjava da se ne boji Božje kazne, nego toga da iznevjeri savez
sections.content:
Vraćajući se psalmu, Grebenar svjedoči da je njegov život blagoslovljen, kao i njegova obitelj, i da je sretan što to može reći. U istom dahu naglašava da se **„jako boji Gospodina“**. Odmah pojašnjava da to nije strah da će ga Bog kazniti. Takvu sliku Boga, tvrdi, nameće đavao jer je sam takav, a „Bog ne želi kažnjavati i ne kažnjava“.

Na pitanje čega se onda boji, voditelj odgovara: boji se da **nije dobra „druga strana“ u savezu između sebe i Boga**. Taj strah objašnjava usporedbom iz obiteljskog života. Jako bi ga pogodilo kad bi mu djeca rekla: „Ti nisi bio dobar tata za nas.“ Jednako bi ga pogodilo kad bi mu supruga rekla da kao muž nije ispunio svoju misiju i zadaću. To bi mu bilo teško upravo zato što su oni „u vjeri i vole Isusa“.

### Kad prijekor postaje „melem za uši“

Sasvim je drukčije, tumači Grebenar, kada isto kaže netko tko nije u vjeri, primjerice rodbina ili krvni srodnici koji žive u smrtnom grijehu i ne obraćaju se unatoč svjedočanstvu. Ako mu takav netko kaže „Ti si me razočarao, nisi čovjek“, on se toga ne boji. Takve bi riječi doživio kao **„melem za uši“** i znak da se ostvaruje Evanđelje. Poziva se na Isusove riječi: **„Tko više ljubi oca ili majku nego mene, nije mene dostojan.“**

Prava težina leži u sudu onoga tko je Božji: brata u Gospodinu koji ljubi Isusa i koji je za Isusa donio neke plodove. Kad bi mu takav rekao „Ti nisi izvršio volju Gospodnju“, toga bi se, priznaje, bojao. „Uvijek je pitanje tko govori“, zaključuje voditelj.
sections.subtitle_en: The fear of God is not the fear of punishment: whose judgment truly has weight
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar explains that he does not fear God's punishment, but rather failing the covenant
sections.content_en:
Returning to the psalm, Grebenar testifies that his life is blessed, as is his family, and that he is happy to be able to say that. In the same breath, he emphasizes that he is **"greatly afraid of the Lord"**. He immediately clarifies that this is not a fear that God will punish him. Such an image of God, he claims, is imposed by the devil because he himself is like that, and "God does not want to punish and does not punish".

When asked what he fears then, the host answers: he fears that **he is not a good "other side" in the covenant between himself and God**. He explains this fear through a comparison from family life. It would hit him very hard if his children told him: "You were not a good dad to us." It would hit him equally hard if his wife told him that as a husband he did not fulfill his mission and task. That would be difficult for him precisely because they are "in the faith and love Jesus".

### When reproach becomes "balm to the ears"

It is completely different, Grebenar explains, when the same is said by someone who is not in the faith, for example relatives or blood relations who live in mortal sin and do not convert despite the witness. If someone like that tells him "You have disappointed me, you are not a human being", he is not afraid of that. He would experience such words as **"balm to the ears"** and a sign that the Gospel is being fulfilled. He refers to the words of Jesus: **"Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me."**

The real weight lies in the judgment of someone who is of God: a brother in the Lord who loves Jesus and who has borne some fruit for Jesus. If such a person told him "You have not done the will of the Lord", he admits he would fear that. "It is always a question of who speaks," the host concludes.

sections.subtitle: Kad se djeca okrenu od vjere: slobodna volja i biblijski primjeri
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj navodi primjer sinova proroka Samuela i svećenika Elija
sections.content:
Iz pitanja „tko govori“ Grebenar prelazi na bolnu temu mnogih roditelja: djecu koja su se, unatoč primljenoj vjeri, „odmetnula i otišla u grijeh“. Podsjeća da dijete ima **slobodnu volju** i može ići kamo želi. „Nismo mi gospodari svoje djece“, kaže. Roditelji ostaju roditelji cijeli život, ali dolazi trenutak kada se sin ili kći osamostaljuju i sami biraju put, bez obzira na vjeru koju su im roditelji prenijeli.

Roditelj je, naglašava voditelj, mogao biti izvrstan i svjedočiti vjeru, a dijete se ipak moglo okrenuti protiv. Takvih primjera ima i u Svetom pismu. **Sinovi proroka Samuela** nisu išli stopama svoga oca, a slično je bilo i sa **sinovima svećenika Elija**. „Kako je to moguće? Ovaj je bio tako velik prorok Samuel, a djeca nisu išla stopama svoga oca. Moguće je. Bog daje slobodan izbor svima“, objašnjava.

Zato roditeljima koji od takve djece čuju „Ti nisi dobar otac“ ili „Ne valjaš“ Grebenar poručuje da im to, „nažalost“, treba biti na radost, jer drukčije ni ne mogu čuti ako su Božji. Neka ih to utješi, kaže, jer mnogi roditelji trpe isto.

Voditelj nabraja i druge prizore koje roditelji proživljavaju: djecu koja čekaju da roditelji umru kako bi podijelila imovinu, djecu bez potomstva te braću i sestre koji međusobno ne razgovaraju. Roditelji se tada pitaju: „Zar su ovo moja djeca?“ Svijet, zaključuje, može utjecati tako da odvoji djecu, pa je zato uvijek važno imati Isusa na prvom mjestu i bojati se Boga tako da ga se ne povrijedi.
sections.subtitle_en: When children turn away from faith: free will and biblical examples
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host cites the example of the sons of the prophet Samuel and the priest Eli
sections.content_en:
From the question "who is speaking", Grebenar moves to the painful topic of many parents: children who, despite the faith they received, "rebelled and went into sin". He reminds that a child has **free will** and can go wherever they want. "We are not masters of our children," he says. Parents remain parents all their lives, but a moment comes when a son or daughter becomes independent and chooses their own path, regardless of the faith their parents passed on to them.

The parent, the host emphasizes, could have been excellent and witnessed to the faith, and yet the child could have turned against it. There are such examples in Sacred Scripture as well. **The sons of the prophet Samuel** did not follow in their father's footsteps, and it was similar with **the sons of the priest Eli**. "How is that possible? This Samuel was such a great prophet, and the children did not follow in their father's footsteps. It is possible. God gives free choice to everyone," he explains.

Therefore, to parents who hear from such children "You are not a good father" or "You are no good", Grebenar says that this, "unfortunately", should be a source of joy to them, because they cannot hear otherwise if they belong to God. May that comfort them, he says, because many parents suffer the same.

The host also lists other scenes that parents experience: children waiting for their parents to die in order to divide the property, children without offspring, and brothers and sisters who do not speak to each other. Parents then ask themselves: "Are these my children?" The world, he concludes, can exert an influence so as to separate children, which is why it is always important to have Jesus in first place and to fear God so as not to hurt Him.

sections.subtitle: „Odlazite od mene, bezakonici“: opomena onima koji samo slave
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar citira Isusove riječi karizmaticima koji su prorokovali i izgonili zle duhove
sections.content:
Najdublji izvor svoga straha Grebenar opisuje kao bojazan da mu Gospodin jednog dana ne kaže: **„Odlazi od mene, bezakoniče.“** Podsjeća na evanđeoski prizor u kojem se ljudi pozivaju na svoje karizme: „Gospodine, Gospodine, zar nismo mi u tvoje ime prorokovali, u tvoje ime čudesa činili, u tvoje ime liječili, zle duhove izgonili?“ Isus im ipak odgovara: „Odlazite od mene, bezakonici.“

Voditelj prepričava kako ga je o tom odlomku upitao „jedan dobar svećenik“: „Brate, kako je to moguće? Što ti misliš o tome?“ Grebenar mu je savjetovao da pročita prethodni dio teksta, u kojem Isus govori o **prokazivanju zla i o tami koja mora biti raskrinkana i iznesena na svjetlo**. Odgovor po njegovu mišljenju leži upravo u tome: ti karizmatici su prešutjeli i **nisu se suprotstavili zlu**. Ostalo je samo „dizanje ruku i slavljenje i ništa više“.

Vršenje volje Božje, tumači Grebenar, obvezuje vjernika da prokazuje zlo i raskrinkava tamu kako bi bila svjetlost. Uz to dodaje ključno ograničenje: **ne raskrinkavati ljude, nego grijeh**. Vjeruje da je to barem djelomično učinio i u ovoj emisiji, govoreći o pastirima, političarima, poduzetnicima i običnim vjernicima koji idu na misu, pričešćuju se i ispovijedaju, a istodobno odobravaju ono što on smatra grijehom.

### „Što me briga što rade u četiri zida“

Voditelj se osvrće na čest stav da se nitko ne treba miješati u to što dvojica muškaraca rade „u četiri zida“. To je, priznaje, djelomično točno: što netko radi u svoja četiri zida, njegov je izbor. Situacija se za njega mijenja kada isti ljudi kažu da žele djecu i da žele **posvojiti djecu koju su roditelji napustili**. Tada se, kaže, kao otac osjeća obveznim reagirati. Tvrdi da bi se tako „na djeci liječile vlastite traume“, uz obrazloženje da „nema nitko tko je izabrao grijeh, a da nije istraumatiziran grijehom“.
sections.subtitle_en: “Depart from me, evildoers”: an admonition to those who only praise
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar quotes Jesus' words to charismatics who prophesied and cast out evil spirits
sections.content_en:
Grebenar describes the deepest source of his fear as the dread that the Lord might one day tell him: **“Depart from me, evildoer.”** He recalls the Gospel scene in which people appeal to their charisms: “Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, perform miracles in your name, heal in your name, cast out evil spirits?” Jesus nevertheless answers them: “Depart from me, evildoers.”

The host recounts how “a good priest” asked him about that passage: “Brother, how is that possible? What do you think about that?” Grebenar advised him to read the preceding part of the text, in which Jesus speaks about **denouncing evil and about the darkness that must be unmasked and brought into the light**. In his view, the answer lies precisely in this: those charismatics remained silent and **did not oppose evil**. All that remained was “raising hands and praising, and nothing more.”

Doing the will of God, Grebenar explains, obligates the believer to denounce evil and unmask darkness so that there may be light. To that he adds a key qualification: **not unmasking people, but sin**. He believes he has done so at least partially in this broadcast as well, speaking about pastors, politicians, entrepreneurs, and ordinary believers who go to Mass, receive Communion, and go to confession, while at the same time approving what he considers sin.

### “Why should I care what they do within four walls”

The host reflects on the frequent attitude that no one should interfere in what two men do “within four walls.” That is, he admits, partially true: what someone does within his four walls is his choice. The situation changes for him when those same people say they want children and want to **adopt children whose parents abandoned them**. Then, he says, as a father he feels obligated to react. He claims that this would amount to “healing one's own traumas on children,” with the explanation that “there is no one who has chosen sin without being traumatized by sin.”

sections.subtitle: Što je grijeh uči Sveto pismo, a ne zakonodavci
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj kritizira parolu „Isus voli sve ljude“ i naglašava da Isus mrzi grijeh
sections.content:
Na pitanje što jest, a što nije grijeh, Grebenar odgovara kratko: **„To uči Sveto pismo i točka.“** Ne određuje to predsjednik države, premijer ni zakonodavci, „ovi što dižu ruku za **Istanbulsku konvenciju** pa idu u crkvu“. Sveto pismo uči, a biskupi i kler ga tumače. Ako tumače dobro, poučavaju narod. Ako ne tumače dobro, upozorava voditelj, mogu narod „strovaliti u pakao, bar tamo gdje djeluju“.

Zato mu je sablažnjivo gledati, kako kaže, zalaganje „ne baš malog broja ljudi“ u Crkvi, pa i u Katoličkoj Crkvi, koji bi trebali raskrinkati i prokazati zlo, a umjesto toga ponavljaju parolu **„Isus voli sve ljude“**. Takvu izjavu u ovom kontekstu naziva licemjernom i izdajničkom. Naravno da Isus voli sve ljude i da je za sve umro na križu, kaže, ali **Isus mrzi grijeh**. Ljudi koji vole grijeh na način da ga se ne žele odreći, tvrdi Grebenar, „zapravo mrze Isusa“.

Kao vrhunac takve logike navodi ideju da bi Crkva, „koja se piše velikim slovom“, mogla otvoriti vrata „sodomskoj katoličkoj molitvenoj zajednici“ osoba u istospolnim zajednicama. To ocjenjuje kao „van svake pameti“.

### Pogled prema Francuskoj i školama

Posljedice, po njegovu mišljenju, već su vidljive u **Francuskoj**, gdje upire prstom u mlade od 15, 16 i 17 godina: „Vidi što si odgojio.“ Podsjeća na svoje iskustvo s predavanja od prije desetak do petnaest godina i dodaje da su takvi, koji su „skočili na njega“, danas učitelji koji odgajaju djecu. U **Hercegovini**, „Bogu hvala“, to nije slučaj, ali „ima toga po Hrvatskoj“.

Prenosi i pritužbe prosvjetnih radnika koji su članovi domoljubne inicijative Ora et labora. Oni se žale da preko političkih veza, primjerice kao rođaci nekog načelnika ili „lokalnog šerifa“, u škole dolaze mladi tek svršeni studenti bez djece, „probušenih noseva, ušiju i jezika“. Voditelj se pita kako takvi mogu odgajati djecu kada ni sami, po njegovim riječima, nisu stekli odgoj.
sections.subtitle_en: Sacred Scripture teaches what sin is, not legislators
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host criticizes the slogan "Jesus loves all people" and emphasizes that Jesus hates sin
sections.content_en:
To the question of what is and what is not sin, Grebenar answers briefly: **"Sacred Scripture teaches that, period."** It is not determined by the president of the state, the prime minister, or legislators, "those who raise their hand for the **Istanbul Convention** and then go to church". Sacred Scripture teaches, and the bishops and clergy interpret it. If they interpret it well, they instruct the people. If they do not interpret it well, the host warns, they can "hurl the people into hell, at least where they operate".

That is why he finds it scandalous to watch, as he says, the advocacy of "not such a small number of people" in the Church, including in the Catholic Church, who should expose and denounce evil, but instead repeat the slogan **"Jesus loves all people"**. He calls such a statement in this context hypocritical and treacherous. Of course Jesus loves all people and died on the cross for everyone, he says, but **Jesus hates sin**. People who love sin in such a way that they do not want to renounce it, Grebenar claims, "actually hate Jesus".

As the culmination of such logic, he cites the idea that the Church, "which is capitalized", could open its doors to a "sodomite Catholic prayer community" of persons in same-sex unions. He assesses that as "out of all mind".

### A look towards France and schools

The consequences, in his opinion, are already visible in **France**, where he points a finger at young people aged 15, 16, and 17: "Look at what you have raised." He recalls his experience from a lecture ten to fifteen years ago and adds that such people, who "jumped on him", are today teachers raising children. In **Hercegovina**, "thank God", that is not the case, but "there is that across Croatia".

He also conveys the complaints of educational workers who are members of the patriotic initiative Ora et labora. They complain that through political connections, for example as relatives of some mayor or "local sheriff", young freshly graduated students without children, with "pierced noses, ears, and tongues", are entering schools. The host wonders how such people can raise children when they themselves, in his words, have not acquired an upbringing.

sections.subtitle: Slavljenje bez suprotstavljanja zlu i osobna odgovornost javnih osoba
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar govori o osobnoj odgovornosti da talente iskoristi za javno suprotstavljanje zlu
sections.content:
Završnu cjelinu ove iteracije Grebenar posvećuje pobožnosti koja ne prelazi u djelovanje. Ako vjernici dižu ruke, slave Isusa i organiziraju duhovne obnove na kojima je „sve lijepo“, a istodobno šute o zlu koje je postalo javno i ne usuđuju se javno mu se suprotstaviti, tada, kaže, **„odgovaramo definiciji bezakonika“**. Šuti se na bezakonje, a „ovamo kao slavimo Isusa“, makar to bila i molitva krunice na trgu ili djelovanje u molitvenim zajednicama.

Tu odgovornost primjenjuje i na sebe. Navodi da vodi molitvenu zajednicu za koju kaže da je trenutno **najveća molitvena zajednica na svijetu koja svaki dan moli i posti**. Opisuje je kao plod autentične **međugorske duhovnosti** u kojoj ljudi uče moliti krunicu i razmatrati Sveto pismo, „pa makar neki škrgutali zubima na to“.

To što ga toliki ljudi slušaju pripisuje milosti Božjoj, a ne vlastitoj pameti, jer mu je Gospodin dao da može tumačiti Sveto pismo. Ističe, međutim, da postoji dio koji ovisi isključivo o njemu. „Osobno ja, Vladimir Grebenar“, kaže, slobodnom voljom biram hoću li talente koje mi je Bog dao koristiti da raskrinkam zlo i suprotstavim mu se. Spreman je, poručuje, da ga udare „bičevi koji su udarali Isusa“, kad već moli „daj mi dio svoje muke i patnje“. Tko tako moli, dodaje, neka ne bude licemjer, nego neka se zlu suprotstavi javno.

### Poziv političarima, poduzetnicima i kleru

Poruku izričito upućuje svima koji djeluju u javnosti:

- **političarima**,
- **poduzetnicima**,
- **voditeljima molitvenih zajednica**,
- **javnim osobama iz klera**.

Od njih se, kaže, očekuje da se **javno konfrontiraju zlu**. Oštro kritizira one koji umjesto toga napadaju upravo one koji to čine, dok sami ostaju „lijepo u četiri zida, gdje je dobar obrok“. Takvi se zatim, prema njegovu opisu, pojavljuju na televiziji i društvenim mrežama „da se njih vidi“, jer im je „došlo pet minuta slave“.
sections.subtitle_en: Praise without opposing evil and the personal responsibility of public figures
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar speaks about the personal responsibility to use talents for public opposition to evil
sections.content_en:
Grebenar dedicates the final part of this iteration to piety that does not turn into action. If believers raise their hands, praise Jesus, and organize spiritual retreats where "everything is nice", while at the same time remaining silent about the evil that has become public and not daring to publicly oppose it, then, he says, **"we fit the definition of the lawless"**. There is silence in the face of lawlessness, while "over here we allegedly praise Jesus", even if it were the praying of the Rosary on a square or activity in prayer communities.

He applies that responsibility to himself as well. He states that he leads a prayer community which he says is currently **the largest prayer community in the world that prays and fasts every day**. He describes it as the fruit of authentic **Međugorje spirituality** in which people learn to pray the Rosary and meditate on Sacred Scripture, "even if some gnash their teeth at that".

The fact that so many people listen to him he attributes to the grace of God, and not to his own intellect, because the Lord granted him that he can interpret Sacred Scripture. He emphasizes, however, that there is a part that depends exclusively on him. "Personally I, Vladimir Grebenar", he says, by free will choose whether I will use the talents that God gave me to unmask evil and oppose it. He is ready, he conveys, to be struck by the "scourges that struck Jesus", since he already prays "give me a part of your passion and suffering". Whoever prays like that, he adds, let him not be a hypocrite, but let him oppose evil publicly.

### A call to politicians, entrepreneurs, and clergy

He explicitly directs the message to all who act in public:

- **politicians**,
- **entrepreneurs**,
- **leaders of prayer communities**,
- **public figures from the clergy**.

From them, he says, it is expected to **publicly confront evil**. He sharply criticizes those who instead attack precisely those who do so, while they themselves remain "nicely within four walls, where there is a good meal". Such people then, according to his description, appear on television and social networks "so that they are seen", because their "five minutes of fame has arrived".
