sections.subtitle: Strah od Božjeg suda: „Gle koliko ljudi nije spašeno zbog tvoje šutnje“
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar govori o strahu da bi mu Bog mogao reći „bezakoniče“ zbog šutnje i pasivnosti
sections.content:
Nastavljajući tumačenje psalma „Blago svakome koji se boji Gospodina“, voditelj **Vladimir Grebenar** opisuje vlastiti strah pred Bogom. Ne boji se kazne, nego Božjeg prijekora. Grebenar priznaje da se jako boji da mu Gospodin jednoga dana ne kaže: **„Bezakoniče, koliki broj ljudi sam poslao da sluša ono zbog čeg sam ti milost dao, a što si ti učinio?“**

U tom zamišljenom Božjem prijekoru on nabraja što bi mu se moglo predbaciti: da mnogi ljudi nisu spašeni zbog njegove šutnje, da je zlo prodrlo ondje gdje je mogao i trebao imati utjecaj, te da je neprijatelj mnogo toga učinio zbog njegove **šutnje, pasivnosti i nerada**. Kao poseban grijeh navodi i **„naslikavanje po društvenim mrežama“** te objave koje, kako kaže, „veze s vezom nemaju“.

Tom mišlju Grebenar zaokružuje prethodni dio tumačenja. U njemu je tvrdio da vjernik koji javno moli i slavi Boga, a šuti pred zlom koje je postalo javno, po njegovu mišljenju odgovara evanđeoskoj definiciji bezakonika.
sections.subtitle_en: Fear of God's judgment: „Look how many people are not saved because of your silence“
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar speaks about the fear that God might tell him „lawless one“ because of silence and passivity
sections.content_en:
Continuing the interpretation of the psalm „Blessed is everyone who fears the Lord“, host **Vladimir Grebenar** describes his own fear before God. He does not fear punishment, but God's reproach. Grebenar admits that he is very afraid that the Lord might one day tell him: **„Lawless one, how many people did I send to listen to that for which I gave you grace, and what did you do?“**

In that imagined God's reproach, he lists what could be reproached against him: that many people are not saved because of his silence, that evil penetrated where he could and should have had influence, and that the enemy did many things because of his **silence, passivity, and inaction**. As a particular sin, he also mentions **„posing on social networks“** and posts that, as he says, „make no sense whatsoever“.

With that thought, Grebenar rounds off the previous part of the interpretation. In it, he asserted that a believer who publicly prays and praises God, but remains silent in the face of evil that has become public, in his opinion corresponds to the Gospel definition of a lawless one.

sections.subtitle: Više žalosti za slavnim pjevačem nego na Veliki petak
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj kritizira javno žalovanje za slavnim osobama na društvenim mrežama
sections.content:
Kao konkretan primjer neprimjerenih objava Grebenar navodi slučaj kad umre neki narodni pjevač ili omiljeni glumac koji nije katolik. To može biti pripadnik druge religije ili drugog naroda, ili netko tko je kršten, ali nije vjernik. Za takvom se osobom, primjećuje voditelj, po društvenim mrežama danima žali, **„čak i od strane nekih koji su u kleru“**.

Citiraju se njezine riječi iz serija ili stihovi pjesama. Grebenar pritom ističe da ni ti filmovi, ni serije, ni glazba nisu proslavljali Isusa, nego su bili „za narodne mase“. Njegov zaključak je oštar: **više je žalosti kad umre neki narodni heroj nego na Veliki petak.**

Posebno ga je pogodila objava u kojoj netko za preminulim piše: **„Bili smo prijatelji.“** Na to se pita: „Kako se Boga ne bojiš to pisati po društvenim mrežama? Bio si prijatelj s nekim tko nije kršćanin.“
sections.subtitle_en: More grief for a famous singer than on Good Friday
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host criticizes public mourning for celebrities on social media
sections.content_en:
As a concrete example of inappropriate posts, Grebenar cites the case when a folk singer or a favorite actor who is not Catholic dies. This can be a member of another religion or another nation, or someone who is baptized, but is not a believer. For such a person, the host notes, there is mourning on social media for days, **"even by some who are in the clergy"**.

Their words from series or song lyrics are quoted. Grebenar emphasizes at the same time that neither those movies, nor series, nor music glorified Jesus, but were "for the masses". His conclusion is sharp: **there is more grief when some folk hero dies than on Good Friday.**

He was particularly struck by a post in which someone writes about the deceased: **"We were friends."** To that he asks: "How do you not fear God writing that on social media? You were friends with someone who is not a Christian."

sections.subtitle: „Bili smo prijatelji“: prijateljstvo koje obvezuje na navještaj
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar postavlja pitanje može li kršćanin zvati prijateljem nekoga kome nije navijestio Krista
sections.content:
Grebenar prelazi na pitanje prijateljstva s pripadnicima drugih religija. Pitanje upućuje svima, a osobito pripadnicima klera. Za njih kaže da bi trebali **„živjeti za Isusa, a ne od Isusa“**. Pita: ako netko ima prijatelja budista, hindusa, muslimana ili ateista i zove ga prijateljem, je li mu Isus doista prijatelj ili to tvrdi samo deklarativno?

Prema njegovu tumačenju, Isus je išao na križ da bi svi postali kršćani katolici i da bi se **„svako koljeno nebesnika, zemnika i podzemnika prignulo“** te priznalo da je Isus Krist Gospodin. Stoga pita je li taj prijatelj kleknuo pred križ i rekao „Ti si Sin Božji“. Možda je umjesto toga samo nudio novac. Kao primjere navodi bogatog hindusa koji oprema katoličku bolnicu, vlasnika kladionice koji oprema crkvu ili nekome od svećenika kupuje automobil.

Ako kršćanin ima prijatelja koji ne prigiba koljena pred Isusom, ne zastaje pred križem, ne ide na misu i ne prima tijelo Kristovo, a nije mu navijestio Krista, Grebenar zaključuje da je takav kršćanin **„totalno zastranio“**. Po njegovim riječima, tada je „gori od najgorih farizeja koji su razapeli Isusa“ i „veća kukavica od apostola koji su pobjegli ispod križa“.

Njegovo je načelo jasno: **„Ako ti nekog zoveš svojim prijateljem, onda tebe to obvezuje da mu navijestiš Krista. To je kršćanstvo na djelu.“** Bez toga, tvrdi, prijateljstva nema.
sections.subtitle_en: “We Were Friends”: Friendship That Obligates to Proclamation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar raises the question of whether a Christian can call someone a friend to whom he has not proclaimed Christ
sections.content_en:
Grebenar moves on to the question of friendship with members of other religions. He addresses the question to everyone, and especially to members of the clergy. About them, he says that they should **“live for Jesus, and not off Jesus”**. He asks: if someone has a Buddhist, Hindu, Muslim, or atheist friend and calls him a friend, is Jesus truly his friend or does he claim that only declaratively?

According to his interpretation, Jesus went to the cross so that everyone would become Catholic Christians and that **“every knee should bend, of those in heaven, on earth, and under the earth”** and confess that Jesus Christ is Lord. Therefore, he asks whether that friend has knelt before the cross and said “You are the Son of God”. Perhaps instead he only offered money. As examples, he cites a wealthy Hindu who equips a Catholic hospital, a betting shop owner who equips a church, or buys a car for one of the priests.

If a Christian has a friend who does not bend his knees before Jesus, does not stop before the cross, does not go to Mass, and does not receive the body of Christ, and he has not proclaimed Christ to him, Grebenar concludes that such a Christian has **“totally gone astray”**. In his words, he is then “worse than the worst Pharisees who crucified Jesus” and “a bigger coward than the apostles who fled from beneath the cross”.

His principle is clear: **“If you call someone your friend, then that obligates you to proclaim Christ to him. That is Christianity in action.”** Without that, he claims, there is no friendship.

sections.subtitle: Jedna rečenica na poslovnom ručku i primjer Majke Tereze
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj navodi primjer Majke Tereze koja je liječila hinduse
sections.content:
Grebenar razlikuje prijateljstvo od kolegijalnog odnosa. S ljudima drugih religija moguće je biti korektan po ljudskim i etičkim standardima, primjerice zbog posla sjesti s njima na ručak. On sam kaže da ima takvo iskustvo. No i u takvim susretima, ističe, Bog nekoga može poslati da mu se posvjedoči. Čovjek možda nikad nije čuo za Isusa, a **„dovoljna je jedna rečenica“**.

To vrijedi i za politiku, gdje se ljudi susreću s onima drugih religija i svjetonazora. Autentični kršćanin dužan je posvjedočiti barem jednom rečenicom da je Kristov. Može to učiniti i znakom, primjerice tako da se **prekriži prije jela** pred sugovornikom. Onome tko druge zove prijateljima, a pritom se predstavlja kao „Kristov laik“ ili „Kristov svećenik“, Grebenar poručuje da ga otkrivaju djela.

Navještaj se, prema voditelju, može dati riječju ili ljubavlju, **kao Majka Tereza**. Ona je liječila i prihvaćala hinduse, a oni su po njoj upoznavali Isusa. Grebenar zatim oblikuje svjedočanstvo kakvo bi vjernik trebao uputiti prijatelju: da je Isus Krist put, da nema drugog spasenja ni drugih spasitelja i da je Isus umro za njega. Dodaje da ga Isus možda ljubi i više nego samog vjernika te da za njegovom dušom žudi. **„Žedan je Isus. Žedan je obraćenja ljudi“**, naglašava voditelj. Kad čovjek tako čuje svjedočanstvo izrečeno iz srca, može se obratiti i reći: „Ja se želim krstiti.“
sections.subtitle_en: One sentence at a business lunch and the example of Mother Teresa
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host cites the example of Mother Teresa who treated Hindus
sections.content_en:
Grebenar distinguishes friendship from a collegial relationship. With people of other religions it is possible to be decent according to human and ethical standards, for example, sitting down for lunch with them because of work. He himself says he has such experience. But even in such encounters, he points out, God can send someone so that a witness may be given to them. A person might never have heard of Jesus, and **"one sentence is enough"**.

This also applies to politics, where people meet those of other religions and worldviews. An authentic Christian is obligated to witness with at least one sentence that he is Christ's. He can also do this with a sign, for example by **making the Sign of the Cross before a meal** in front of the interlocutor. To someone who calls others friends while presenting himself as "Christ's layman" or "Christ's priest", Grebenar says that works reveal him.

The proclamation, according to the host, can be given by word or by love, **like Mother Teresa**. She treated and accepted Hindus, and through her they came to know Jesus. Grebenar then formulates the kind of witness a believer should address to a friend: that Jesus Christ is the way, that there is no other salvation nor other saviors, and that Jesus died for him. He adds that Jesus perhaps loves him even more than the believer himself and that He yearns for his soul. **"Jesus is thirsty. He is thirsty for the conversion of people"**, the host emphasizes. When a person hears such a witness spoken from the heart, he can convert and say: "I want to be baptized."

sections.subtitle: Kad prijatelj odbije: „Ti si u zabludi“, i teškoće mješovitih brakova
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar objašnjava zašto se sakramentalni brakovi s pripadnicima drugih religija teško održe
sections.content:
Što ako takozvani prijatelj odgovori da poštuje njegovo uvjerenje, ali da je kršćanstvo „samo jedna od ponuda“, a on kao hindus, budist ili musliman ima svoje? Grebenar odgovara da je vjernik tada dužan reći mu: **„Gle, ti si u zabludi.“**

Kao usporedbu navodi praksu Katoličke Crkve u pitanju braka. Da bi primili sakrament vjenčanja, muškarac i žena trebaju biti katolici. Voditelj spominje i iznimke, kad je jedna strana druge religije, ali smatra da se takvi savezi **„u pravilu raspadaju vrlo brzo“**. Civilni brak može trajati desetljećima, no ustrajanje u sakramentalnom životu, kaže, „jako je rijetko“. Jedna strana prevlada, druga se mora prilagoditi ili brak pukne. Priznaje da ni sam nije čuo za suprotan slučaj.

Zato, poručuje, treba biti potpuno izravan i govoriti istinu onako kako je zapisana u Svetom pismu, bez priča o „progresu“ svijeta. Ironično se osvrće na Francusku, „zemlju prosvjetiteljstva, znanosti, napretka“, i na prizore mladih iz Pariza. „Bože nas sačuvaj takvih mladih u hrvatskom narodu“, kaže. Ako bi takva bila mladost u Hrvatskoj, zaključuje, „neće više biti Hrvatske“.
sections.subtitle_en: When a friend rejects: "You are in error", and the difficulties of mixed marriages
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar explains why sacramental marriages with members of other religions are difficult to maintain
sections.content_en:
What if a so-called friend replies that he respects his belief, but that Christianity is "just one of the offers", while he, as a Hindu, Buddhist, or Muslim, has his own? Grebenar replies that the believer is then obliged to tell him: **"Look, you are in error."**

As a comparison, he cites the practice of the Catholic Church regarding marriage. In order to receive the sacrament of marriage, a man and a woman must be Catholics. The host also mentions exceptions, when one party is of another religion, but considers that such unions **"as a rule fall apart very quickly"**. A civil marriage can last for decades, but perseverance in sacramental life, he says, is "very rare". One side prevails, the other must adapt, or the marriage breaks up. He admits that he himself has not heard of the opposite case.

Therefore, he says, one should be completely direct and speak the truth as it is written in Sacred Scripture, without stories about the "progress" of the world. He ironically reflects on France, the "land of the Enlightenment, science, progress", and on the scenes of young people from Paris. "God save us from such youth among the Croatian people", he says. If the youth in Croatia were like that, he concludes, "there will no longer be a Croatia".

sections.subtitle: Isusove posljednje riječi kao zapovijed na vratima svakog doma
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj naglašava težinu Isusovih posljednjih riječi prije uzašašća
sections.content:
Sve proizlazi iz straha Božjega, naglašava Grebenar. Tko se boji Boga, navijestit će Krista „takozvanom prijatelju“, a on će sam odlučiti hoće li Isusa prihvatiti ili odbaciti. Za mjerilo voditelj ne uzima mišljenja „nekih bibličara i liberalnih teologa“, nego Isusove vlastite riječi, i to one posljednje, izrečene pred uzašašće.

Težinu posljednjih riječi ilustrira osobnim iskustvom. Sjeća se posljednjih riječi svoje pokojne bake prije nego što je izdahnula: „To sam svojim očima vidio, to se ne zaboravlja.“ Podsjeća i kako svi pozorno slušaju mladence kad se na svadbi obraćaju gostima, ili umirućega kad se oprašta od bližnjih.

Isusove posljednje riječi, smatra Grebenar, trebale bi **„pisati na svim ulazima u sve stambene zgrade, u stanove, u kuće“**, jer nisu pozdravne, nego su zapovijed. Isus se, objašnjava, ne oprašta od učenika, nego kaže: „Ostajem s vama u sve dane do svršetka svijeta. Neću vas ostaviti siročad.“ Odlazi u tijelu, ali se vraća kroz euharistiju i na druge načine. S prijestolja slave milost dolazi u euharistiju, ispovijed i Crkvu, po rukama svećenika.
sections.subtitle_en: Jesus' last words as a commandment on the doors of every home
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host emphasizes the weight of Jesus' last words before the ascension
sections.content_en:
Everything stems from the fear of God, emphasizes Grebenar. Whoever fears God will proclaim Christ to a "so-called friend," and he will decide for himself whether he will accept or reject Jesus. As a standard, the host does not take the opinions of "certain biblical scholars and liberal theologians," but Jesus' own words, specifically the last ones, spoken before the ascension.

He illustrates the weight of last words with personal experience. He remembers the last words of his late grandmother before she breathed her last: "I saw that with my own eyes, that is not forgotten." He also recalls how everyone listens attentively to the newlyweds when they address the guests at a wedding, or to a dying person when saying goodbye to loved ones.

Jesus' last words, Grebenar believes, should **"be written on all entrances to all residential buildings, into apartments, into houses"**, because they are not farewell words, but are a commandment. Jesus, he explains, does not say goodbye to the disciples, but says: "I remain with you all days until the end of the world. I will not leave you orphans." He leaves in the body, but returns through the Eucharist and in other ways. From the throne of glory, grace comes into the Eucharist, confession, and the Church, through the hands of the priest.

sections.subtitle: „Idite po svem svijetu“: vjera i krštenje kao uvjet spasenja
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar citira Isusovu zapovijed „Idite po svem svijetu i propovijedajte evanđelje“
sections.content:
Središnja zapovijed glasi: **„Idite po svem svijetu i propovijedajte evanđelje.“** Grebenar posebno ističe dva uvjeta za spasenje koja Isus navodi: **povjerovati i pokrstiti se**. Prema njegovu tumačenju, Isus nije rekao da je dovoljno samo povjerovati, a krštenje je sporedno. Tko je povjerovao, mora se i krstiti.

Za one koji ne povjeruju Isus, nastavlja voditelj, kaže samo da će biti osuđeni. Krštenje tu više ne spominje, jer onaj tko nije povjerovao nema ni razloga krstiti se. „O, gle Isusa kako je radikalan, a bio na križu“, primjećuje Grebenar. Dodaje da Isus i Otac nebeski cijene žrtvu na križu, „samo je ne cijene mnogi koji dobro žive od Isusa“.

Na pitanje zašto bi Isus bio tako strog Grebenar odgovara Isusovim riječima: zato što **„nisu povjerovali u jedinorođenoga Sina Božjega“**. „Točka, nema dalje“, zaključuje. Tko nije prignuo koljeno pred Isusom Kristom, prema njegovu tumačenju, ne može se spasiti.
sections.subtitle_en: "Go into all the world": faith and baptism as a condition of salvation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar quotes Jesus' command "Go into all the world and preach the gospel"
sections.content_en:
The central command reads: **"Go into all the world and preach the gospel."** Grebenar particularly emphasizes two conditions for salvation that Jesus states: **to believe and to be baptized**. According to his interpretation, Jesus did not say that it is enough only to believe, and baptism is secondary. Whoever has believed must also be baptized.

For those who do not believe, Jesus, the host continues, says only that they will be condemned. Baptism is no longer mentioned here, because the one who has not believed has no reason to be baptized either. "Oh, look at Jesus, how radical he is, and yet he was on the cross," remarks Grebenar. He adds that Jesus and the Heavenly Father value the sacrifice on the cross, "only many who make a good living off Jesus do not value it."

To the question of why Jesus would be so strict, Grebenar answers with Jesus' words: because **"they have not believed in the only-begotten Son of God"**. "Period, that's it," he concludes. Whoever has not bowed the knee before Jesus Christ, according to his interpretation, cannot be saved.

sections.subtitle: „Kršćanstvo je samo jedna od ponuda“ i samoizopćenje heretika
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj kritizira tezu neimenovanog crkvenog velikodostojnika da je kršćanstvo samo jedna od ponuda
sections.content:
Grebenar zatim oštro kritizira, ne navodeći ime, „vrlo omiljenog crkvenog velikodostojnika“. Za njega kaže da je popularan na lijevo-liberalnim društvenim mrežama i u medijima, a da je izjavio kako je **„kršćanstvo samo jedna od ponuda“**. Takvog velikodostojnika, prema voditelju, slave oni koji su kršteni, ali „nisu upoznali milost Božju“, i suprotstavljaju ga „radikalnima i konzervativnima“.

Voditelj takvu tezu naziva herezom i poručuje da je treba javno i otvoreno raskrinkati, umjesto da se „ljube ručice“ iz poštovanja. Takav pristup, prema njegovu mišljenju, otvara vrata LGBT-u. **„Poštuju se oni koji poštuju Isusa“**, kaže Grebenar. Oni koji ne poštuju jedinorođenoga Sina Božjega i njegov križ, po njegovu tumačenju, **sami su sebe izopćili**, bez obzira na ruho koje nose. „Ne treba ti to nitko ni reći. Naučavaš hereze, zavodiš narod, sam sebe si ekskomunicirao“, kaže, i dodaje da takvih slučajeva ima mnogo.
sections.subtitle_en: "Christianity is only one of the offers" and self-excommunication of heretics
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host criticizes the thesis of an unnamed church dignitary that Christianity is only one of the offers
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then sharply criticizes, without mentioning a name, a "very popular church dignitary." About him he says that he is popular on left-liberal social networks and in the media, and that he stated that **"Christianity is only one of the offers."** Such a dignitary, according to the host, is celebrated by those who are baptized, but "have not come to know the grace of God," and contrast him with the "radicals and conservatives."

The host calls such a thesis heresy and says that it should be publicly and openly exposed, instead of "kissing little hands" out of respect. Such an approach, in his opinion, opens the door to LGBT. **"Those who respect Jesus are respected,"** says Grebenar. Those who do not respect the only-begotten Son of God and his cross, according to his interpretation, **have excommunicated themselves**, regardless of the vestments they wear. "No one even needs to tell you that. You teach heresies, you mislead the people, you have excommunicated yourself," he says, and adds that there are many such cases.

sections.subtitle: Koncerti u korizmi, žalovanje dijela klera i istina u lice farizejima
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar govori o koncertima u korizmi i Velikom tjednu i reakcijama dijela klera
sections.content:
Vraćajući se primjeru preminulog pjevača, Grebenar priznaje da ga je ta situacija zaboljela. Riječ je o omiljenom izvođaču iz drugog naroda i druge religije. Za njega se isticalo da je „pomagao katolicima“, a istodobno je, prema voditelju, održavao koncerte po katoličkim gradovima Hrvatske i Bosne i Hercegovine **za vrijeme korizme, pa čak i u Velikom tjednu**, kad katolici, kako naglašava, ne smiju ići na koncerte.

Grebenar kaže da ga „boli srce“ što su neki iz klera po društvenim mrežama za tim pjevačem iskazivali žalost veću nego za samim Gospodinom na Veliki petak. To su, po njegovim riječima, oni koji objavljuju „lijepe sličice nepoznatih autora“. Takve naziva zavodnicima koji propovijedaju i vode političke emisije, a njihovu duhovnost opisuje kao **„duhovnost zavisti“** koja, prema njegovu tumačenju, nije od Boga.

Na pitanje kako se odnositi prema farizejima odgovara: onako kako je to činio Isus, **„treba im reći istinu u lice, licemjeri“**. Svoju poruku završava pitanjem: „Bojite se svijeta, bojite se đavla, a ne bojite se Gospodina. Pa koji duh te vodi ako se Boga ne bojiš?“
sections.subtitle_en: Concerts in Lent, the mourning of part of the clergy, and the truth to the faces of the Pharisees
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar speaks about concerts in Lent and Holy Week and the reactions of part of the clergy
sections.content_en:
Returning to the example of the deceased singer, Grebenar admits that this situation hurt him. It is about a beloved performer from another nation and another religion. It was pointed out about him that he „helped Catholics“, while at the same time, according to the host, he held concerts across Catholic cities of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina **during Lent, and even in Holy Week**, when Catholics, as he emphasizes, must not go to concerts.

Grebenar says that „his heart hurts“ that some from the clergy expressed greater sorrow on social media for that singer than for the Lord Himself on Good Friday. Those are, according to his words, the ones who post „pretty little pictures by unknown authors“. He calls such people seducers who preach and host political shows, and describes their spirituality as a **„spirituality of envy“** which, according to his interpretation, is not from God.

To the question of how to relate to the Pharisees, he answers: the way Jesus did, **„one must tell them the truth to their face, hypocrites“**. He ends his message with the question: „You fear the world, you fear the devil, and you do not fear the Lord. So what spirit leads you if you do not fear God?“

sections.subtitle: Evanđelje dana i dva razloga zašto Isus govori u prispodobama
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj čita evanđelje o gorušičinu zrnu i kvascu
sections.content:
Nakon psalma Grebenar čita evanđelje dana: **„Čemu je slično kraljevstvo Božje? Ono je kao kad čovjek uze gorušičino zrno i baci ga u svoj vrt. Uzraste i razvi se u stablo te mu se ptice nebeske gnijezde po granama.“** Druga prispodoba glasi: kraljevstvo je **„kao kad žena uze kvasac i zamijesi ga u tri mjere brašna dok sve ne uskisne“**.

Voditelj objašnjava da Isus i narodu i farizejima govori u prispodobama iz dva razloga. Prvi je da ih ne razumiju oni koji su „sinovi tame“, pomračenog, racionalnog i „strogo ortodoksnog“ duha. Drugi je da ih razumiju oni otvorena srca, jer im usporedba otvara oči. Takav čovjek tada kaže: „Aha, sad sam shvatio. Ovo mijenja moj odnos prema tome.“

Zato su prispodobe jednima zagonetka, a drugima **riječ spoznaje**. Grebenar ih uspoređuje s **nožem ili mačem koji reže** odnos između čovjeka i nekog pojma ili događaja. Prispodoba, kaže, ili uvelike zbuni ili prosvijetli.
sections.subtitle_en: Gospel of the day and two reasons why Jesus speaks in parables
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host reads the Gospel about the mustard seed and the yeast
sections.content_en:
After the psalm, Grebenar reads the Gospel of the day: **„What is the kingdom of God like? It is like when a man took a mustard seed and cast it into his garden. It grew and developed into a tree, and the birds of the air nest in its branches.“** The second parable goes: the kingdom is **„like when a woman took yeast and mixed it into three measures of flour until all of it was leavened“**.

The host explains that Jesus speaks in parables to both the people and the Pharisees for two reasons. The first is so that those who are „sons of darkness“, of a darkened, rational, and „strictly orthodox“ spirit, do not understand them. The second is so that those with an open heart understand them, because the comparison opens their eyes. Such a person then says: „Aha, now I understand. This changes my relationship toward that.“

That is why parables are a riddle to some, and to others **a word of knowledge**. Grebenar compares them to a **knife or a sword that cuts** the relationship between a person and a certain concept or event. A parable, he says, either greatly confuses or enlightens.

sections.subtitle: Kontrolabilnost kao grijeh lažnog katoličanstva
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar objašnjava pojam „kontrolabilnosti“ preuzet iz poslovnog svijeta
sections.content:
Kako bi opisao duh koji ne razumije prispodobe, Grebenar posuđuje pojam iz poslovnog svijeta: **kontrolabilnost**. Riječ je o katolicima koji bi kontrolirali druge, pa i samog Isusa i Duha Svetoga. Takav sustav uspoređuje s nacizmom i „najmračnijim komunizmom“, u kojima nema rasprave i ne smije se slobodno pitati.

Navodi i riječi jednog čovjeka koji mu je rekao da je **„dobio PTSP od tih kontrola“**. Grebenar to smatra razumljivim i kaže da je takvo iskustvo „gore nego da meci fijuču oko tvoje glave“. Čovjek dođe raditi na Božjoj njivi, stvoren da kroz njega govori „ričući lav, Krist Gospodin“, a dočeka ga zabrana: „Nećeš ti pričati meni o Isusu.“

Kontrolabilnost naziva **„užasom i grijehom današnjeg lažnog katoličanstva“**. Suprotstavlja joj Isusove riječi: **„Ne brani, tko nije protiv nas, za nas je.“**
sections.subtitle_en: Controllability as a Sin of False Catholicism
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar explains the concept of "controllability" borrowed from the business world
sections.content_en:
In order to describe the spirit that does not understand parables, Grebenar borrows a concept from the business world: **controllability**. It is about Catholics who would control others, even Jesus Himself and the Holy Spirit. He compares such a system to Nazism and "the darkest communism," in which there is no debate and one is not allowed to ask freely.

He also cites the words of a man who told him that he **"got PTSD from those controls"**. Grebenar considers this understandable and says that such an experience is "worse than bullets whizzing around your head." A man comes to work in God's field, created so that "the roaring lion, Christ the Lord" might speak through him, and is met with a prohibition: "You are not going to talk to me about Jesus."

He calls controllability **"the horror and sin of today's false Catholicism"**. He contrasts it with Jesus' words: **"Do not forbid him, whoever is not against us is for us."**

sections.subtitle: Pravi brat pomaže, lažni vreba, a jedini branitelj bio je razbojnik
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pripovijeda o dobrom razbojniku koji je jedini obranio Isusa na križu
sections.content:
Grebenar suprotstavlja dva duha. **Farizejski duh** sluša, ali je zbunjen i ne razumije. **Apostolski duh**, duh svetaca, otvoren je za Božju riječ, post, molitvu, evangelizaciju i obraćenja. Raduje se kad čuje da se nekome promijenio život.

Odatle izvodi sliku **pravog brata**. Kad brat ili sestra koji su uspješni u evangelizaciji padnu ili pogriješe, pravi brat moli za njih, priskače im u pomoć i ohrabruje ih. Opominje ih dobronamjerno, a onaj tko primi opomenu zahvaljuje Bogu što su mu se „otvorile oči“. **Lažni brat**, nasuprot tome, čeka i vreba, kao što su farizeji vrebali Isusa na riječi. Osudili su ga unaprijed jer je prokazivao tamu, pakost i zavist njihovih srca. Takva su srca, kaže voditelj, toliko podmukla da „možeš umirati pored njega, neće ti ruku pružiti“.

Na vrhuncu te slike nalazi se Kalvarija. Prema jednom od evanđelja, kako navodi Grebenar, oba su se razbojnika najprije rugala Isusu. No kad je jedan vidio količinu mržnje i prezira prema Isusu, obratio se. Taj „dobri razbojnik“, naglašava voditelj, nije bio dobar, i sam je priznao: „Mi smo ovdje zaslužili da visimo na križu, ali Isus nije.“ **Od svih prisutnih, uključujući farizeje koji su poučavali narod o vjeri, Isusa je obranio samo razbojnik.** Zato, zaključuje Grebenar, Isus farizejima kaže: „Pretekoše vas bludnice i carinici u kraljevstvo Božje.“
sections.subtitle_en: A true brother helps, a false one lurks, and the only defender was a thief
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host narrates about the good thief who was the only one to defend Jesus on the cross
sections.content_en:
Grebenar contrasts two spirits. The **Pharisaic spirit** listens, but is confused and does not understand. The **apostolic spirit**, the spirit of the saints, is open to God's word, fasting, prayer, evangelization, and conversions. It rejoices when it hears that someone's life has changed.

From there he draws the image of the **true brother**. When a brother or sister who is successful in evangelization falls or errs, the true brother prays for them, rushes to their aid, and encourages them. He admonishes them with good intentions, and the one who receives the admonition thanks God that his "eyes were opened." The **false brother**, by contrast, waits and lurks, just as the Pharisees lurked for Jesus at His word. They condemned Him in advance because He exposed the darkness, malice, and envy of their hearts. Such hearts, says the host, are so insidious that "you can be dying next to him, he will not extend a hand to you."

At the climax of that image is Calvary. According to one of the Gospels, as Grebenar states, both robbers initially mocked Jesus. But when one saw the amount of hatred and contempt toward Jesus, he converted. That "good thief," emphasizes the host, was not good, and he himself admitted: "We here deserved to hang on the cross, but Jesus did not." **Of all those present, including the Pharisees who taught the people about faith, only the thief defended Jesus.** That is why, concludes Grebenar, Jesus says to the Pharisees: "Prostitutes and tax collectors preceded you into the kingdom of God."

sections.subtitle: Egzorcizam nad samim sobom: tjerati farizeja iz vlastitog srca
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar govori o vođenju velike inicijative bez duha kontrole
sections.content:
Tko se boji Boga, ističe Grebenar, tražit će farizeja u sebi. Takvi ljudi **„rade egzorcizam sami nad sobom“**. Iz sebe tjeraju farizejsku vjeru razuma, kontrolu nad drugima i uvjerenje da sve ovisi o njima i da se njih mora sve pitati, „kao Bog“.

Voditelj to povezuje s vlastitim iskustvom vodstva. Bio je direktor u velikoj tvrtki, a danas vodi veliku domoljubnu inicijativu s mnogo ljudi. Kaže da ne želi takav duh. Priznaje da se o važnim i velikim odlukama mora pitati i da on za neke stvari mora znati. No kad mu netko s osmijehom dođe i kaže da je u molitvi dobio poticaj nešto pokrenuti, moliti ili postiti, to se, prema njegovim riječima, ne smije spriječiti. Tada srce gori: „Vidi kako je Bog zahvatio njegovo srce. Bože, proslavi se.“

Za svakoga nudi i test: **„Da li se ja Boga bojim?“** Tko se boji da mu Bog ne kaže „bezakoniče“, zaključuje, na dobrom je putu i otjerao je od sebe duh farizejštine.
sections.subtitle_en: Exorcism over oneself: casting the Pharisee out of one's own heart
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar speaks about leading a large initiative without the spirit of control
sections.content_en:
Whoever fears God, Grebenar emphasizes, will look for the Pharisee within himself. Such people **“perform an exorcism over themselves”**. They drive out of themselves the Pharisaic faith of reason, control over others, and the conviction that everything depends on them and that they must be consulted about everything, “like God”.

The host connects this with his own experience of leadership. He was a director in a large company, and today he leads a large patriotic initiative with many people. He says he does not want such a spirit. He admits that he must be consulted about important and big decisions and that he must know about certain things. But when someone comes to him with a smile and says that in prayer they received an impulse to initiate something, pray, or fast, that, according to his words, must not be prevented. Then the heart burns: “Look how God has taken hold of his heart. God, be glorified.”

He also offers a test for everyone: **“Do I fear God?”** Whoever fears lest God say to him “lawless one”, he concludes, is on the right path and has driven away from himself the spirit of Pharisaism.

sections.subtitle: Gorušičino zrno i kvasac: Bog djeluje kroz neznatno, skriveno i strpljivo
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači sliku gorušičina zrna koje nitko ne vidi
sections.content:
Grebenar potom tumači same prispodobe. Gorušičino je zrno toliko sitno i neznatno da ga nitko ne vidi, a ako padne, ne može se naći. Bog, objašnjava voditelj, djeluje upravo kroz ono što u ljudskim očima nema vrijednost. Podsjeća na pitanje: **„Iz Nazareta, može li što dobro izaći?“** Bog daje znakove i potvrde, ali ne nužno spektakularne. Oni se razlučuju i spoznaju duhom i srcem. Otvorenima se otkrivaju, a drugima ne znače ništa.

Zrno raste skriveno od očiju svijeta i treba mu vremena. Nitko ne zna što je dok ne proklija i ne pusti lišće. Tada izraste u stablo u kojem se ptice gnijezde. Ptice su, prema Grebenarovu tumačenju, **slika anđela i svetih koji dolaze služiti**.

Druga prispodoba, o kvascu, govori o vremenu. Žena zamijesi tijesto i ostavi ga preko noći. Na njemu ne radi, nego „Bog radi s njim nešto“. **„Za nešto veliko, vrijedno, važno, ukusno, pravo mora proći vrijeme“**, naglašava voditelj. Primjer je sam Isus, koji je **30 godina u skrovitosti radio s Josipom u radionici**. Ni susjedi nisu znali da je Mesija dok nije došlo vrijeme i dok nije rekao da se ostvarilo Pismo. Čak je i apostolima zaprijetio da to ne govore dok ne dođe trenutak. Pitanje „Jesi li ti Mesija?“, primjećuje Grebenar, dugo je ostalo otvoreno.
sections.subtitle_en: The mustard seed and leaven: God acts through the insignificant, hidden, and patient
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host interprets the image of the mustard seed that no one sees
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then interprets the parables themselves. The mustard seed is so tiny and insignificant that no one sees it, and if it falls, it cannot be found. God, the host explains, acts precisely through what has no value in human eyes. He recalls the question: **"Can anything good come out of Nazareth?"** God gives signs and confirmations, but not necessarily spectacular ones. They are discerned and known by the spirit and the heart. To the open they are revealed, while to others they mean nothing.

The seed grows hidden from the eyes of the world and needs time. No one knows what it is until it sprouts and puts forth leaves. Then it grows into a tree in which birds nest. The birds are, according to Grebenar's interpretation, **an image of angels and saints who come to serve**.

The second parable, about the leaven, speaks of time. A woman kneads the dough and leaves it overnight. She does not work on it, but "God is doing something with it". **"For something great, valuable, important, tasty, genuine, time must pass"**, the host emphasizes. An example is Jesus Himself, who **for 30 years in hiddenness worked with Joseph in the workshop**. Not even the neighbors knew that He was the Messiah until the time came and until He said that the Scripture was fulfilled. He even strictly warned the apostles not to speak of it until the moment came. The question "Are you the Messiah?", Grebenar notes, remained open for a long time.

sections.subtitle: Članstvo u Ora et labora: strpljivost i bez obvezne članarine
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj poziva na učlanjenje u inicijativu i naglašava da je članstvo besplatno
sections.content:
Grebenar poziva gledatelje da postanu članovi **domoljubne inicijative Ora et labora**. Pritom traži strpljivost i povezuje je s upravo protumačenim evanđeljem: zrno mora rasti, tijesto se mora dići, a „ne ide to za tri minute“. Sve što je vrijedno za kraljevstvo Božje, kaže, traži vremena, kao što ga traži podizanje obitelji ili stjecanje zvanja.

Za one s otvorenim pitanjima na ekranu su istaknuti brojevi mobitela za Hrvatsku i za Bosnu i Hercegovinu. Voditelj ističe da je podrška inicijativi **potpuno dobrovoljna**. Član se može postati **bez članarine i bez donacije**. „Ne znam gdje još ima da možeš biti član, a ne moraš ništa dati“, kaže. Kritičare koje naziva farizejima, a koji tvrde da on ljudima naplaćuje članarine, otpravlja riječima: „Jad i beda.“
sections.subtitle_en: Membership in Ora et labora: patience and no mandatory membership fee
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host invites viewers to join the initiative and emphasizes that membership is free
sections.content_en:
Grebenar invites viewers to become members of the **patriotic initiative Ora et labora**. In doing so, he asks for patience and connects it to the Gospel that was just explained: the seed must grow, the dough must rise, and “it doesn't happen in three minutes.” Everything that is valuable for the kingdom of God, he says, requires time, just as raising a family or obtaining a profession requires it.

For those with open questions, mobile phone numbers for Hrvatska and for Bosna i Hercegovina are highlighted on the screen. The host emphasizes that support for the initiative is **completely voluntary**. One can become a member **without a membership fee and without a donation**. “I don't know where else it exists that you can be a member, and you don't have to give anything,” he says. Critics whom he calls Pharisees, and who claim that he charges people membership fees, he dismisses with the words: “Misery and wretchedness.”

sections.subtitle: Svjedočanstva o ozdravljenjima: rijetka bolest i nalazi bolji za 50 posto
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar čita svjedočanstva vjernica o ozdravljenjima
sections.content:
Pri kraju emisije Grebenar čita svjedočanstva gledateljica. **Božana** piše da je njezin muž ozdravio od autoimune bolesti. Bolest je bila toliko rijetka da je, prema njezinim riječima, u cijeloj Njemačkoj imalo oko 800 oboljelih. „Nisam ni sumnjala jer toliko čuda Božjih sam doživjela. Isus moj, sve moje, moj početak, moj kraj“, poručuje. Voditelj objašnjava da Isus daje takve znakove kako bi čovjek spoznao da je Bog s njim i u njemu.

**Tereza** svjedoči o sestri koja je, unatoč karcinomu dojke, postila pet dana. Govorili su joj da to nije za nju, a ona je odgovorila: **„Ja sam pozvana i odazivam se.“** Nakana joj je bila zdravlje sina, kojemu su loše vrijednosti na bubrezima i prijeti mu odstranjivanje bubrega. Tijekom posta osjećala je više snage i energije. Sin joj je potom javio da su mu **sve vrijednosti u krvi i urinu pale za više od 50 posto**. „Suze radosnice su potekle“, piše Tereza, i zahvaljuje Bogu, Isusu, Mariji, Duhu Svetom i svetom Josipu.

Grebenar zahvaljuje na svjedočanstvima i podsjeća na još jednu Isusovu posljednju riječ: **„Bit ćete mi svjedoci do na kraj svijeta.“** Dodaje da se, Božjom milošću, zajedničkim molitvama i postovima, ovaj podcast čuje „do na kraj svijeta“.
sections.subtitle_en: Testimonies of healings: a rare disease and test results better by 50 percent
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar reads female faithful's testimonies about healings
sections.content_en:
Near the end of the show, Grebenar reads testimonies from female viewers. **Božana** writes that her husband was healed of an autoimmune disease. The disease was so rare that, according to her words, there were about 800 sufferers in all of Germany. "I didn't even doubt because I have experienced so many of God's miracles. My Jesus, my all, my beginning, my end," she conveys. The host explains that Jesus gives such signs so that man may come to know that God is with him and in him.

**Tereza** testifies about her sister who, despite breast cancer, fasted for five days. They told her that this was not for her, and she answered: **"I am called and I respond."** Her intention was the health of her son, who has poor kidney values and faces the removal of a kidney. During the fast, she felt more strength and energy. Her son then informed her that **all his values in blood and urine dropped by more than 50 percent**. "Tears of joy flowed," Tereza writes, and thanks God, Jesus, Mary, the Holy Spirit, and Saint Joseph.

Grebenar gives thanks for the testimonies and recalls another final word of Jesus: **"You will be my witnesses to the ends of the earth."** He adds that, by God's grace, through common prayers and fasts, this podcast is heard "to the ends of the earth."

sections.subtitle: Poziv muškarcima na trgove, blagoslov i centar Kraljica Mira u Međugorju
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj poziva muškarce na javnu molitvu krunice na trgovima
sections.content:
Grebenar upućuje poziv **muškarcima iz Njemačke i Austrije** na javnu molitvu krunice **u Zagrebu 7. studenoga**. Muškarce u Hrvatskoj i Bosni i Hercegovini poziva da pokrenu molitvu krunice na trgu u svom gradu ili općini. Ako im to ne dopuste, neka mole kraj crkve ili, kako duhovito dodaje, „u šumi kao partizani“. Prenosi i savjet jednog svećenika: ako ne daju moliti na trgu, neka po dvojica šeću trgom i mole, jer to im nitko ne može zabraniti. To je njihov intiman razgovor s Isusom, a „gdje su dvojica ili trojica sabrani u moje ime, ja sam tu“. Na taj se način, prema Grebenaru, na trgovima lome prokletstva zla o kojima je govorio u tumačenju.

Nakon završnog blagoslova voditelj podsjeća da se kupnjom prve, druge i treće knjige **„Isus lider“** pomaže dovršetak **Međunarodnog edukacijskog centra Kraljica Mira u Međugorju**. Riječ je o njegovu privatnom projektu u koji ulaže i osobni novac. Naglašava da ne gradi hotel ni restorane i da ne živi od turizma. Gradi prostor potreban za evangelizaciju, a „Bog zna zašto, pokazat će vrijeme“. Zahvaljuje svima koji su knjigu kupili s tom namjerom. Dodaje i da su se mnogi obratili čitajući „Isus lider“, bez obzira na to koji su dio čitali. Emisiju zatvara pozivom da se Ora et labora prati svaki dan, „na veću slavu Božju“.
sections.subtitle_en: Call to men to the squares, blessing, and the Kraljica Mira center in Međugorje
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host calls men to the public prayer of the Rosary on squares
sections.content_en:
Grebenar extends a call to **men from Germany and Austria** to the public prayer of the Rosary **in Zagreb on November 7**. He calls men in Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina to start praying the Rosary on the square in their city or municipality. If they are not allowed to do so, let them pray near the church or, as he humorously adds, “in the forest like partisans”. He also conveys the advice of a priest: if they are not allowed to pray on the square, let them walk across the square in pairs and pray, because no one can forbid them that. That is their intimate conversation with Jesus, and “where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I”. In this way, according to Grebenar, the curses of evil that he spoke about in the interpretation are broken on the squares.

After the final blessing, the host reminds that purchasing the first, second, and third book **“Isus lider”** helps complete the **Međunarodni edukacijski centar Kraljica Mira in Međugorje**. It is his private project in which he also invests personal money. He emphasizes that he is not building a hotel or restaurants and that he does not live off tourism. He is building a space needed for evangelization, and “God knows why, time will tell”. He thanks everyone who bought the book with that intention. He also adds that many have converted reading “Isus lider”, regardless of which part they read. He closes the show with a call to follow Ora et labora every day, “for the greater glory of God”.

iterations.theme_en: The duty of proclaiming Christ, the parables of the mustard seed and yeast, and announcements and testimonies
